subtopics.name: Exactly solvable lattice models
subtopics.scope: Classical two-dimensional and quantum one-dimensional lattice models (vertex, Potts, dimer, hard-hexagon, spin chains) whose free energies, order parameters, or spectra can be obtained in closed form.

subtopics.name: Critical phenomena and renormalization group
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium continuous phase transitions in O(N), Potts, and related models in general dimension, focusing on universality classes, critical exponents, crossover behavior, and multicritical points.

subtopics.name: Conformal and field-theoretic methods in low dimensions
subtopics.scope: Continuum field-theory treatments of critical and quasi-ordered systems in one and two dimensions and at boundaries or defects in higher dimensions, including conformal field theory and the Coulomb gas, bosonization and Luttinger liquids, Kosterlitz-Thouless and defect-mediated melting transitions, entanglement scaling at quantum critical points, integrable perturbed field theories, and SLE or loop-model descriptions of critical geometry.

subtopics.name: Mean-field spin glasses and replica symmetry breaking
subtopics.scope: Ising, p-spin, spherical, and Potts spin-glass models with fully connected or sparse random couplings, their thermodynamics, ergodicity breaking, and energy-landscape complexity.

subtopics.name: Quenched disorder, pinning, and avalanches
subtopics.scope: Statistical mechanics of finite-dimensional systems with quenched randomness, covering random-field, diluted, and short-range spin-glass models, Harris and Imry-Ma criteria, Griffiths and infinite-randomness phases, elastic manifolds pinned by random media and their depinning transitions, and disorder-driven hysteresis, avalanches, and crackling noise.

subtopics.name: Percolation and geometric phase transitions
subtopics.scope: Connectivity transitions of random clusters on lattices, continua, and random graphs, including thresholds, cluster-size statistics, fractal dimensions, and variants such as bootstrap, continuum, and explosive percolation.

subtopics.name: Statistical mechanics of neural networks and learning
subtopics.scope: Typical-case analysis of associative memories and of learning in perceptrons, committee machines, and wide or deep networks, focusing on storage capacity, generalization curves, and high-dimensional training dynamics.

subtopics.name: Random constraint satisfaction and high-dimensional inference
subtopics.scope: Phase transitions in random combinatorial optimization and planted inference problems such as satisfiability, coloring, matching, community detection, and compressed sensing.

subtopics.name: Spectra of random matrices and operators
subtopics.scope: Eigenvalue densities, spacing statistics, extreme eigenvalues, and eigenvector properties of random matrix ensembles, including sparse, structured, and non-Hermitian ones.

subtopics.name: Anderson and many-body localization
subtopics.scope: Localization of waves and quantum particles by disorder or quasiperiodicity, from single-particle mobility edges and multifractal critical states to interacting many-body localization.

subtopics.name: Quantum quenches and isolated-system thermalization
subtopics.scope: Nonequilibrium dynamics of isolated quantum many-body systems after quenches, covering thermalization, generalized Gibbs ensembles, entanglement growth, and generalized hydrodynamics of integrable chains.

subtopics.name: Driven lattice gases and nonequilibrium transport
subtopics.scope: Boundary-driven and bulk-driven stochastic particle and energy transport models, such as exclusion and zero-range processes and oscillator chains, focusing on steady states, currents, phase diagrams, and anomalous conduction.

subtopics.name: Interfaces, wetting, and stochastic growth
subtopics.scope: Statistical mechanics of fluctuating interfaces and growing surfaces, at equilibrium and away from it, including roughening and wetting transitions, capillary-wave and solid-on-solid models, kinetic roughening in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang, Edwards-Wilkinson and conserved (MBE) growth classes, directed polymers in random media, and fractal or Laplacian growth such as diffusion-limited aggregation.
subtopics.broadened_from: KPZ interface growth and directed polymers

subtopics.name: Stochastic processes, anomalous diffusion, and large deviations
subtopics.scope: Statistical properties of random walks, Brownian and Langevin dynamics, and anomalous diffusion, such as Lévy flights, continuous-time random walks and fractional Brownian motion, analyzed through Fokker–Planck and master equations, including first-passage and search problems, extreme-value and record statistics, large deviations of path functionals, and stochastic resetting, without the energetics of stochastic thermodynamics.
subtopics.broadened_from: Random walks, first passage, and extremes

subtopics.name: Stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation relations
subtopics.scope: Thermodynamics of small systems driven out of equilibrium, including entropy production, work and heat fluctuations, uncertainty relations, efficiency of microscopic engines, and the thermodynamics of information.

subtopics.name: Active matter and self-propelled particles
subtopics.scope: Statistical mechanics of particles that consume energy to self-propel, covering run-and-tumble and active Brownian dynamics, motility-induced phase separation, flocking, and active pressure and boundary accumulation.

subtopics.name: Coarsening, aging, and phase-ordering kinetics
subtopics.scope: Relaxation of systems quenched into ordered or critical phases, including domain-growth laws, dynamical scaling, autocorrelation exponents, aging, and kinetic Ising and voter dynamics.

subtopics.name: Absorbing states, spreading, and population dynamics
subtopics.scope: Nonequilibrium phase transitions and collective kinetics in stochastic many-agent systems, covering absorbing-state transitions (directed percolation, contact processes, sandpile self-organized criticality), diffusion-limited reaction kinetics, epidemic and information spreading on lattices and complex networks, voter and opinion-dynamics models, evolutionary game dynamics, and stochastic population, extinction, and ecological competition models.

subtopics.name: Glasses, jamming, and amorphous solids
subtopics.scope: Structural glass formation and jamming of disordered packings, including mean-field theories in infinite dimensions, mode-coupling dynamics, random first-order transitions, kinetically constrained models, and marginal stability.

subtopics.name: Classical fluids and kinetic theory
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium and transport properties of classical fluids and hard-core gases, including virial coefficients, integral-equation and density-functional theories, exactly solvable one-dimensional fluids, and Boltzmann-equation kinetics of molecular and granular gases.

subtopics.name: Polymers, self-avoiding walks, and lattice paths
subtopics.scope: Statistics of polymer chains and lattice path ensembles, including self-avoiding walks, adsorption and collapse transitions, stretched polymers, vesicles, and enumeration of lattice animals.

subtopics.name: Long-range interactions and synchronization
subtopics.scope: Systems with long-range or all-to-all couplings, including Hamiltonian mean-field and self-gravitating models, ensemble inequivalence, quasi-stationary states, and Kuramoto-type synchronization of coupled oscillators.

techniques.name: Transfer matrices and duality transformations
techniques.scope: Writing partition functions as traces of transfer-matrix powers and using Kramers-Wannier-type dualities to obtain free energies, correlation lengths, and exact critical points.

techniques.name: Coordinate and algebraic Bethe ansatz
techniques.scope: Diagonalizing integrable Hamiltonians and transfer matrices via Bethe equations, then extracting ground-state energies, excitation spectra, and thermodynamic-Bethe-ansatz thermodynamics in the thermodynamic limit.

techniques.name: Free-fermion, Pfaffian, and dimer mappings
techniques.scope: Mapping spin chains, planar Ising models, or dimer coverings onto quadratic fermion problems (Jordan-Wigner, Kasteleyn Pfaffians) to compute spectra, correlations, and entanglement exactly.

techniques.name: Replica method with symmetry breaking
techniques.scope: Averaging the logarithm of disordered partition functions via replicas and evaluating the saddle point under replica-symmetric or Parisi-type ansatze to obtain free energies, thresholds, and stability lines.

techniques.name: Cavity method and message passing
techniques.scope: Solving models on sparse random graphs or dense factor graphs through cavity recursions, belief propagation, state evolution, and population dynamics to obtain thresholds and typical-case observables.

techniques.name: Perturbative field-theoretic renormalization group
techniques.scope: Computing beta functions, fixed points, and critical exponents to fixed order in epsilon or 1/N expansions from Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson and related continuum actions.

techniques.name: Real-space and strong-disorder renormalization
techniques.scope: Decimation, Migdal-Kadanoff, and strong-disorder renormalization schemes that produce recursion relations whose fixed points give exact or approximate critical couplings and exponents.

techniques.name: Conformal field theory and Coulomb gas
techniques.scope: Using conformal and modular invariance and Coulomb-gas mappings to determine scaling dimensions, finite-size amplitudes, boundary exponents, and critical correlation functions in two dimensions.

techniques.name: Saddle-point and large-N asymptotics
techniques.scope: Evaluating partition functions, generating functions, and integrals asymptotically via Laplace and steepest-descent methods in spherical, O(N)-vector, mean-field, and other large-parameter limits.

techniques.name: Response-field path integrals and dynamical mean-field theory
techniques.scope: Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-De Dominicis and Doi-Peliti functional integrals, and the dynamical mean-field equations they yield, for Langevin and stochastic reaction dynamics of interacting or disordered systems.

techniques.name: Exact solution of master equations
techniques.scope: Solving master, Fokker-Planck, and backward Kolmogorov equations exactly via generating functions, eigenfunction expansions, and image methods to obtain stationary states and time-dependent distributions.

techniques.name: Renewal theory and Laplace-transform methods
techniques.scope: Using renewal equations, Laplace transforms, and Sparre Andersen or Pollaczek-Spitzer formulas to obtain first-passage, survival, record, and resetting statistics of stochastic processes.

techniques.name: Large deviations and tilted generators
techniques.scope: Computing rate functions and scaled cumulant generating functions of empirical and time-integrated observables via tilted generators, Gartner-Ellis and contraction principles, and macroscopic fluctuation theory.

techniques.name: Matrix product ansatz for steady states
techniques.scope: Representing nonequilibrium steady states of stochastic lattice models as products of matrices obeying quadratic algebras to compute currents, density profiles, correlations, and phase diagrams.

techniques.name: Resolvent and free-probability methods
techniques.scope: Determining spectral densities, edges, and extreme eigenvalues of random matrices and operators via Stieltjes transforms, self-consistent resolvent equations, R- and S-transforms, and log-gas energy minimization.

techniques.name: Cluster, virial, and series expansions
techniques.scope: Mayer cluster, virial, high- and low-temperature, and exact-enumeration series expansions combined with ratio or Pade analysis to obtain thermodynamic coefficients, thresholds, and critical exponents.

subtopics.name: Bound-state QED and exotic atoms
subtopics.scope: Relativistic, recoil, radiative and finite-nuclear-size corrections to energy levels of hydrogen, helium, positronium, muonic and antiprotonic atoms.

subtopics.name: Many-electron atomic structure and field effects
subtopics.scope: Relativistic and many-body calculation and measurement of energy levels, fine and hyperfine structure, isotope shifts, oscillator strengths and radiative lifetimes of atoms and highly charged ions, and of how they respond to external fields, including static and dynamic polarizabilities, Stark and Zeeman shifts, magic wavelengths and blackbody shifts.
subtopics.broadened_from: Atomic polarizabilities and field-induced level shifts

subtopics.name: Dispersion forces and Casimir-Polder interactions
subtopics.scope: Van der Waals, retarded Casimir-Polder and resonant interactions between atoms, molecules and surfaces, including dispersion coefficients and thermal or nonequilibrium effects.

subtopics.name: Photoionization and electron-atom scattering
subtopics.scope: Single- and multiphoton ionization cross sections, angular distributions, autoionizing resonances and low-energy electron or positron scattering from atoms and ions.

subtopics.name: Strong-field, attosecond and ultrafast electron dynamics
subtopics.scope: Interaction of intense and ultrashort laser pulses with atoms, molecules and clusters, covering tunnel, multiphoton and nonsequential multiple ionization, above-threshold ionization and electron rescattering, high-harmonic and attosecond pulse generation, attosecond streaking and pump-probe tracking of electron motion and charge migration, laser-induced electron diffraction, and strong-field molecular alignment, dissociation and Coulomb explosion.

subtopics.name: Rydberg atoms and dipole blockade
subtopics.scope: Highly excited atomic states, their scaling laws, long-range dipolar and van der Waals interactions, blockade, facilitation and Rydberg dressing.

subtopics.name: Spectral line shapes and pressure broadening
subtopics.scope: Natural, Doppler, collisional and transit-time broadening, line-shape profiles, Dicke narrowing and line mixing in atomic and molecular gases.

subtopics.name: Molecular rovibrational structure and spectroscopy
subtopics.scope: Rotational, vibrational, fine and hyperfine structure of diatomic and polyatomic molecules, including anharmonic potentials, Hund's cases, intensities and selection rules.

subtopics.name: Nonadiabatic dynamics and conical intersections
subtopics.scope: Breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, vibronic coupling, geometric phases, Jahn-Teller and Renner-Teller effects, and radiationless transitions in molecules.

subtopics.name: Chemical reaction rates and tunneling
subtopics.scope: Transition-state, instanton, Kramers and Marcus theories of thermal reaction and transfer rates, including quantum tunneling corrections and isotope effects.

subtopics.name: Solvable model systems in electronic structure
subtopics.scope: Exactly or quasi-exactly solvable few-electron models used to benchmark quantum-chemical approximations and exact conditions of density-functional theory.

subtopics.name: Ultracold collisions, molecules and few-body physics
subtopics.scope: Low-energy atom-atom, atom-ion, atom-molecule and molecule-molecule scattering and its control: Feshbach and shape resonances, multichannel quantum defect theory, photoassociation and magnetoassociation of ultracold molecules, collisional shielding and cold controlled chemistry, inelastic and sticky-collision loss, and universal few-body physics such as Efimov states, three-body recombination and few-body bound states in reduced dimensions.

subtopics.name: Bose-Einstein condensates: mean-field and excitations
subtopics.scope: Gross-Pitaevskii dynamics, Bogoliubov spectra, collective modes, vortices, solitons and beyond-mean-field corrections in trapped Bose gases.

subtopics.name: Spinor and dipolar quantum gases
subtopics.scope: Quantum gases with internal spin degrees of freedom, synthetic spin-orbit coupling, or long-range anisotropic dipolar interactions, including their phases, spin dynamics and roton excitations.

subtopics.name: Strongly interacting Fermi gases and pairing
subtopics.scope: BCS-BEC crossover, unitary Fermi gas thermodynamics, spin-imbalanced and mass-imbalanced mixtures, Tan contact relations and Fermi polarons.

subtopics.name: Quantum simulation with lattice-confined ultracold atoms
subtopics.scope: Theory and experiment on ultracold atoms in optical lattices and other engineered periodic potentials used as quantum simulators of condensed-matter models, covering band structure and Bose- and Fermi-Hubbard physics, Mott and superfluid phases, quantum magnetism and superexchange, Floquet engineering, synthetic dimensions and artificial gauge fields, topological bands and Chern numbers, disorder and many-body localization, quantum gas microscopy, and nonequilibrium transport and quench dynamics in lattices.

subtopics.name: One-dimensional integrable quantum gases
subtopics.scope: Lieb-Liniger, Yang-Gaudin and Tonks-Girardeau gases, their thermodynamics and correlations, and their nonequilibrium dynamics in one dimension.

subtopics.name: Laser cooling and optical forces
subtopics.scope: Doppler, sub-Doppler and sideband cooling limits, radiation pressure, optical dipole traps and magneto-optical trapping of atoms and molecules.

subtopics.name: Trapped-ion motion and entangling gates
subtopics.scope: Motional modes of ion crystals in Paul and Penning traps, Lamb-Dicke physics, sideband transitions and spin-motion entangling gates.

subtopics.name: Coherent atomic media and optical pumping
subtopics.scope: Electromagnetically induced transparency, coherent population trapping, slow light, optical pumping and atomic magnetometry in multilevel atomic ensembles.

subtopics.name: Precision measurement with clocks and interferometers
subtopics.scope: Optical and microwave atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic or molecular searches for electric dipole moments, varying constants and new forces.

subtopics.name: Cavity QED and Jaynes-Cummings models
subtopics.scope: Coupling of atoms or artificial atoms to quantized cavity modes, including vacuum Rabi splitting, photon blockade, and the Rabi, Tavis-Cummings and Dicke models.

subtopics.name: Waveguide QED and collective emission
subtopics.scope: Emitters coupled to one-dimensional or structured photonic continua, including superradiance, subradiance and cooperative scattering in atomic arrays.

subtopics.name: Open quantum systems and master equations
subtopics.scope: Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics of driven dissipative quantum systems, covering decoherence, resonance fluorescence and nonequilibrium steady states.

subtopics.name: Quantum states of light and photonic information
subtopics.scope: Quantum optical field theory and photonic quantum information: preparing, characterizing and using nonclassical states of light (squeezed, Fock, cat, and entangled photon pairs), including Glauber coherence theory, phase-space quasiprobability distributions, photodetection, homodyne tomography, photon-counting statistics, multiphoton interference and boson sampling in linear optical networks, continuous-variable entanglement and teleportation, linear-optical quantum computing, and quantum communication protocols with photons.

subtopics.name: Optomechanics and macroscopic mechanical quantum systems
subtopics.scope: Coupling of light, microwaves and embedded spins or atoms to mechanical degrees of freedom across cavity, Brillouin and levitated-particle platforms. It covers ground-state and feedback cooling, optomechanically induced transparency, mechanical squeezing and entanglement, nonlinear and multimode optomechanical dynamics, quantum-limited force and displacement sensing, and tests of macroscopic quantum superpositions.

subtopics.name: Quantum measurement, estimation and sensing theory
subtopics.scope: Theory and protocols for extracting information from quantum systems: Fisher-information precision bounds for estimating parameters with entangled, squeezed or adaptively controlled probes under noise, quantum sensing schemes, state and process tomography, state discrimination and hypothesis testing, and weak or generalized measurements with their back-action limits.

subtopics.name: Nonlinear optics and optical solitons
subtopics.scope: Parametric and Kerr processes, phase matching, harmonic generation, modulational instability, and soliton propagation in fibers and waveguides.

subtopics.name: Photonic lattices and periodic structures
subtopics.scope: Photonic crystals, coupled waveguide arrays and metamaterials, including band gaps, edge states and parity-time-symmetric gain-loss structures.

subtopics.name: Light scattering, plasmonics and metamaterials
subtopics.scope: Electromagnetic scattering and absorption by particles, nanostructures, rough surfaces and disordered media, including Mie theory, multiple scattering and light transport in random media, together with surface plasmon polaritons, near-field optics, nanoantennas, metamaterials and metasurfaces, negative refraction, transformation optics, and how nanostructured surroundings change the emission of nearby sources.

subtopics.name: Beam propagation, diffraction and polarization optics
subtopics.scope: Paraxial and nonparaxial propagation of Gaussian and orbital-angular-momentum beams, diffraction, partial coherence, and polarization transformations.

subtopics.name: Laser theory and resonator dynamics
subtopics.scope: Semiclassical and quantum laser theory, including thresholds, linewidths, relaxation oscillations, mode locking and optical resonator modes.

techniques.name: Sum-over-states perturbation theory
techniques.scope: Rayleigh-Schrödinger and Dalgarno-Lewis perturbation theory for level shifts, polarizabilities and dispersion coefficients, evaluated in closed form or as rapidly converging sums.

techniques.name: Adiabatic elimination and effective Hamiltonians
techniques.scope: Schrieffer-Wolff transformations and elimination of fast or far-detuned states to obtain effective couplings, light shifts, superexchange and two-photon Rabi frequencies.

techniques.name: Lindblad master equations and quantum regression
techniques.scope: Solving Markovian master equations for steady states, decay rates, fluorescence spectra, and two-time correlation functions via the quantum regression theorem.

techniques.name: Input-output theory and quantum Langevin equations
techniques.scope: Linearized Heisenberg-Langevin equations with input-output relations to compute transmission spectra, noise spectra, squeezing and cooling limits.

techniques.name: Bogoliubov diagonalization and linear stability
techniques.scope: Diagonalizing quadratic bosonic or fermionic Hamiltonians and linearizing nonlinear equations about stationary solutions to obtain excitation spectra, instability thresholds and growth rates.

techniques.name: Partial-wave and zero-range scattering theory
techniques.scope: Phase shifts, effective-range expansions and Bethe-Peierls contact conditions to obtain cross sections, bound-state energies, resonance positions and threshold laws.

techniques.name: Born-Oppenheimer and hyperspherical adiabatic methods
techniques.scope: Separation of fast and slow coordinates to obtain effective potentials, nonadiabatic couplings and universal scaling laws in molecules and few-body systems.

techniques.name: WKB and semiclassical quantization
techniques.scope: Bohr-Sommerfeld and WKB approximations with connection formulas to obtain bound-state spectra, tunneling rates, level densities and quantum defects.

techniques.name: Saddle-point and stationary-phase asymptotics
techniques.scope: Asymptotic evaluation of integrals in a large parameter to obtain ionization rates, harmonic cutoffs, diffraction patterns and semiclassical amplitudes.

techniques.name: Floquet theory and high-frequency expansions
techniques.scope: Quasienergy spectra of periodically driven systems, with Magnus and high-frequency expansions to derive effective static Hamiltonians and renormalized couplings.

techniques.name: Electromagnetic Green's tensors and mode expansions
techniques.scope: Dyadic Green's functions and normal-mode expansions to compute radiative rates, Lamb shifts, Casimir-Polder potentials and dipole-dipole couplings near material structures.

techniques.name: Coupled-mode theory and transfer matrices
techniques.scope: Coupled-amplitude equations and transfer or scattering matrices for waveguides, multilayers, periodic media and resonator networks, giving dispersion relations and transmission spectra.

techniques.name: Phase-space and Gaussian-state methods
techniques.scope: Wigner, P and Q quasiprobability distributions and the covariance-matrix formalism, used to quantify squeezing, entanglement and noise in continuous-variable systems.

techniques.name: Quantum Fisher information and estimation bounds
techniques.scope: Computing quantum and classical Fisher information to derive Cramér-Rao precision limits, optimal probe states and optimal measurements.

techniques.name: Landau-Zener and adiabatic passage analysis
techniques.scope: Exactly solvable time-dependent level-crossing models and adiabaticity criteria to obtain transition probabilities and the efficiency of population transfer, as in STIRAP and rapid adiabatic passage.

techniques.name: Variational and Thomas-Fermi mean-field methods
techniques.scope: Gaussian or trial-wavefunction variational ansätze, Thomas-Fermi limits and self-consistent gap equations for ground-state properties, phase boundaries and collective-mode frequencies.

techniques.name: Bethe ansatz and exact integrability
techniques.scope: Exact solution of integrable many-body and impurity models through Bethe equations, giving energies, thermodynamics, excitation spectra and correlation properties.

techniques.name: Angular-momentum algebra and irreducible tensors
techniques.scope: Wigner-Eckart theorem, 3j and 6j symbols, and spherical-tensor decompositions for deriving selection rules, line strengths, angular distributions and tensor level shifts.

subtopics.name: Bethe-ansatz solvable quantum many-body models
subtopics.scope: Exact spectra, thermodynamics, finite-size effects and correlation functions of quantum integrable models such as XXZ, Hubbard, Lieb-Liniger and Gaudin, solved by coordinate, algebraic or nested Bethe ansatz.

subtopics.name: Integrable nonlinear PDEs and dispersive waves
subtopics.scope: Continuous integrable systems and nonlinear dispersive wave equations (KdV, NLS, sine-Gordon, KP, Camassa-Holm and their hierarchies), including inverse scattering and Riemann-Hilbert methods, Hirota bilinear and tau-function theory, bi-Hamiltonian structures, finite-gap and algebro-geometric solutions, Whitham modulation and dispersive shock waves, soliton interactions and rogue waves, and perturbations of integrable wave equations close to the integrable case.
subtopics.broadened_from: Solitons and the inverse scattering transform

subtopics.name: Discrete integrable systems and lattice equations
subtopics.scope: Integrable difference and differential-difference equations, birational maps and ultradiscrete systems, characterised by multidimensional consistency, singularity confinement and low algebraic entropy.

subtopics.name: Painlevé equations and isomonodromic deformations
subtopics.scope: Painlevé transcendents and their discrete and higher-order analogues: special solutions, connection formulae, asymptotics, tau functions and isomonodromic Hamiltonian structure.

subtopics.name: Superintegrable and separable Hamiltonian systems
subtopics.scope: Classical and quantum Hamiltonian systems with extra integrals of motion or separable coordinates (Calogero-Moser, Kepler-type, Stäckel systems), their polynomial symmetry algebras and exact spectra.

subtopics.name: Lie symmetry analysis of differential equations
subtopics.scope: Point, contact, nonlocal and Noether symmetries of ordinary and partial differential equations, used to classify equations, build conservation laws and find invariant solutions.

subtopics.name: Random matrices, free probability and determinantal processes
subtopics.scope: Random matrix theory in its full breadth: eigenvalue statistics of Hermitian, non-Hermitian and structured ensembles (including Coulomb-gas and β-ensembles), local universality and Dyson Brownian motion, free probability and large-N asymptotics, matrix models with genus expansions and topological recursion, determinantal and Pfaffian point processes, products of random matrices and Lyapunov exponents, and random-matrix descriptions of quantum chaos, excluding orthogonal-polynomial theory itself, Painlevé analysis, KPZ growth models and spin glasses.
subtopics.broadened_from: Random matrix ensembles and eigenvalue statistics

subtopics.name: Exactly solved lattice models in statistical mechanics
subtopics.scope: Two-dimensional lattice models (Ising, Potts, six- and eight-vertex, dimers, hard hexagons) solved with transfer matrices, the Yang-Baxter equation, Pfaffians or corner transfer matrices.

subtopics.name: Interacting particle systems and KPZ universality
subtopics.scope: Exactly solvable stochastic particle systems and growth models (ASEP, TASEP, zero-range processes, directed polymers) analysed with integrable-probability tools.

subtopics.name: Mean-field spin glasses and disordered models
subtopics.scope: Free energies, phase transitions and ground-state properties of disordered mean-field models (Sherrington-Kirkpatrick, p-spin, random energy model, perceptron) and related random optimisation problems.

subtopics.name: Random Schrödinger operators and localization
subtopics.scope: Spectral and transport properties of Schrödinger and Jacobi operators with random or quasi-periodic potentials, including Anderson localization, Lyapunov exponents and the integrated density of states.

subtopics.name: Schrödinger operator spectra and eigenvalue bounds
subtopics.scope: Bound states, eigenvalue counting, resonances and sharp spectral inequalities (Lieb-Thirring, Hardy, CLR) for Schrödinger, Dirac and magnetic operators.

subtopics.name: Spectral geometry and quantum graphs
subtopics.scope: Eigenvalues of Laplace-type operators on domains, manifolds and metric graphs: Weyl asymptotics, isospectrality, nodal counts, eigenvalue optimisation and the effect of boundary or vertex conditions.

subtopics.name: Heat kernels, zeta functions and Casimir energies
subtopics.scope: Spectral functions of Laplace-type operators (heat-kernel coefficients, zeta-regularised determinants) and the vacuum (Casimir) energies of fields in bounded or topologically nontrivial geometries.

subtopics.name: Quantum fields in curved spacetime
subtopics.scope: Particle creation, vacuum polarisation, Hawking and Unruh effects, and renormalised stress tensors of quantum fields on black-hole, de Sitter and cosmological backgrounds.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

subtopics.name: Exact solutions and perturbations in gravity
subtopics.scope: Exact solutions of Einstein and modified-gravity field equations and their linear perturbations: black holes, horizons, geodesic motion, quasinormal modes and stability.

subtopics.name: Conformal field theory and infinite-dimensional algebras
subtopics.scope: Conformal field theories in two and higher dimensions and the algebraic structures behind them, including Virasoro, affine Kac-Moody and W-algebra representation theory, vertex operator algebras and modular forms, conformal blocks and crossing equations, the conformal bootstrap, boundary and defect CFT, and logarithmic and non-unitary CFTs.
subtopics.broadened_from: Two-dimensional conformal field theory and VOAs

subtopics.name: Exact results in supersymmetric gauge theories
subtopics.scope: Exact partition functions, indices, BPS spectra and prepotentials of supersymmetric gauge theories obtained from localization, Seiberg-Witten geometry and dualities.

subtopics.name: Scattering amplitudes and Feynman integrals
subtopics.scope: Analytic evaluation and structure of perturbative scattering amplitudes and multiloop Feynman integrals: polylogarithms, elliptic integrals, symbols, recursion relations and differential equations.

subtopics.name: Topological field theories and knot invariants
subtopics.scope: Chern-Simons and other topological quantum field theories, their partition functions, link and three-manifold invariants, and the associated quantum-group and modular-category structures.

subtopics.name: Topological solitons in classical field theory
subtopics.scope: Kinks, vortices, monopoles, instantons and skyrmions in classical field theories: BPS bounds, moduli spaces, energies, interactions and topological charges.

subtopics.name: Exactly solvable and non-Hermitian quantum mechanics
subtopics.scope: Exactly and quasi-exactly solvable potentials, supersymmetric quantum mechanics, shape invariance, exceptional orthogonal polynomials, and PT-symmetric or pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonians.

subtopics.name: Semiclassical asymptotics, WKB and resurgence
subtopics.scope: Semiclassical and large-order behaviour in quantum mechanics and field theory: WKB and exact WKB, instantons, Borel summability, trans-series and resurgent structure.

subtopics.name: Open quantum systems and Lindblad dynamics
subtopics.scope: Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics of quantum systems coupled to environments: GKLS generators, quantum channels, steady states, spectral gaps and exactly solvable dissipative models.

subtopics.name: Orthogonal polynomials and special functions
subtopics.scope: Classical, q- and multivariate orthogonal polynomials and hypergeometric-type special functions: recurrences, asymptotics, zeros, generating functions and their algebraic structures (Askey-Wilson, Racah).

subtopics.name: Mean-field and kinetic limits of many-body systems
subtopics.scope: Derivation and analysis of effective equations (Hartree, Gross-Pitaevskii, Vlasov, Boltzmann) and Bogoliubov corrections for large interacting quantum and classical particle systems, including stability of matter.

techniques.name: Coordinate and algebraic Bethe ansatz
techniques.scope: Diagonalise integrable Hamiltonians or transfer matrices through Bethe equations, then get ground-state energies, excitations and finite-size corrections in the thermodynamic limit from root densities or nonlinear integral equations.

techniques.name: Riemann-Hilbert analysis and nonlinear steepest descent
techniques.scope: Recast a problem as a matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem and deform its contours (Deift-Zhou method) to obtain explicit leading and subleading asymptotics.

techniques.name: Hirota bilinear and Darboux-Bäcklund constructions
techniques.scope: Build explicit multi-soliton, breather, rational and determinant solutions from bilinear forms, tau functions and Darboux, Bäcklund or dressing transformations.

techniques.name: Transfer-matrix and Lyapunov exponent methods
techniques.scope: Write partition functions or one-dimensional eigenproblems as products of transfer matrices, whose leading eigenvalues or growth rates give free energies, correlation lengths or localization lengths.

techniques.name: Saddle-point and large-N asymptotics
techniques.scope: Evaluate integrals by Laplace and steepest-descent methods, including equilibrium measures and Coulomb-gas variational problems, to obtain leading and subleading large-parameter behaviour.

techniques.name: WKB, matched asymptotics and Borel resummation
techniques.scope: Use singular-perturbation expansions with turning-point connection formulas, boundary-layer matching, and Borel or Padé analysis of divergent series.

techniques.name: Perturbation theory and renormalization-group flow
techniques.scope: Expand order by order (Feynman diagrams or Rayleigh-Schrödinger) with regularisation to get beta functions, anomalous dimensions, fixed points and critical exponents.

techniques.name: Integration-by-parts and differential equations for integrals
techniques.scope: Reduce families of parametric integrals to master integrals and solve the resulting Picard-Fuchs or canonical differential equations, supplemented by Mellin-Barnes representations.

techniques.name: Spectral zeta functions and heat-kernel expansions
techniques.scope: Compute regularised determinants, vacuum energies and anomalies from zeta functions, Mellin transforms and heat-kernel asymptotic coefficients.

techniques.name: Toeplitz and Fredholm determinant asymptotics
techniques.scope: Express gap probabilities, emptiness formation, entanglement and correlation functions as Toeplitz, Hankel or Fredholm determinants and evaluate them with Szegő and Fisher-Hartwig asymptotics.

techniques.name: Replica and cavity methods
techniques.scope: Average over disorder with replicated partition functions or message-passing self-consistency, using replica-symmetric or symmetry-broken ansätze to obtain free energies and thresholds.

techniques.name: Representation theory and character formulas
techniques.scope: Use the representation theory of Lie (super)algebras, quantum groups and the Virasoro algebra (Casimirs, branching rules, Weyl-Kac characters, fusion) to obtain spectra, degeneracies and multiplicities.

techniques.name: Separation of variables and special functions
techniques.scope: In adapted coordinates, reduce linear PDEs or eigenvalue problems to ODEs solved by hypergeometric, Heun, Bessel or Mathieu functions, with spectra fixed by quantisation or boundary conditions.

techniques.name: Variational principles and sharp inequalities
techniques.scope: Derive optimal constants and exact bounds from min-max characterisations, trial states, Euler-Lagrange equations, and rearrangement or Sobolev-type inequalities.

techniques.name: Linear stability and normal-mode analysis
techniques.scope: Linearise around exact solutions to get eigenvalue problems, and compute their spectra (quasinormal frequencies, instability thresholds, bifurcation points) analytically or with shooting or spectral numerics.

techniques.name: Generating functions and exact enumeration
techniques.scope: Encode counting problems, partition functions and moments in generating functions, Pfaffians or Kasteleyn matrices, then use kernel and transfer methods to extract closed forms and asymptotic growth constants.

subtopics.name: Scattering amplitudes and on-shell methods
subtopics.scope: Structure and computation of gauge-theory and gravity scattering amplitudes at tree and loop level using on-shell techniques instead of Feynman diagrams.

subtopics.name: Conformal bootstrap and CFT data
subtopics.scope: Constraints on operator dimensions and OPE coefficients of conformal field theories in more than two dimensions from crossing symmetry, unitarity and the analytic structure of correlators.

subtopics.name: Two-dimensional CFT and modular invariance
subtopics.scope: Virasoro and extended chiral algebras, minimal and rational models, torus and boundary partition functions, and modular bootstrap constraints in two-dimensional conformal field theory.

subtopics.name: Gauge/gravity duality and holographic models
subtopics.scope: AdS/CFT computations of correlators, transport coefficients, phase structure and entanglement in strongly coupled field theories from classical bulk gravity solutions.

subtopics.name: Supersymmetric gauge dynamics and localization
subtopics.scope: Exact non-perturbative results in supersymmetric gauge theories obtained from holomorphy, Seiberg-Witten geometry, dualities, supersymmetric indices and localization of path integrals.

subtopics.name: Integrability in gauge and string theories
subtopics.scope: Integrable structures in spin chains, two-dimensional sigma models and planar N=4 super Yang-Mills and AdS strings, solved exactly with Bethe ansatz and S-matrix methods.

subtopics.name: String compactifications and flux vacua
subtopics.scope: Four-dimensional effective theories obtained from Calabi-Yau, orbifold, orientifold and flux compactifications of string theory, including spectra, moduli stabilization and vacuum structure.

subtopics.name: Generalized symmetries and quantum anomalies
subtopics.scope: Perturbative and global anomalies, anomaly matching and inflow, and higher-form and non-invertible symmetries as constraints on the dynamics and phases of quantum field theories.

subtopics.name: Topological solitons, instantons and monopoles
subtopics.scope: Classical and semiclassical properties of kinks, vortices, monopoles, skyrmions and instantons, including BPS bounds, moduli spaces, fluctuation spectra and tunneling amplitudes.

subtopics.name: Matrix models, SYK and two-dimensional gravity
subtopics.scope: Large-N matrix and vector models, Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev-type disordered models, and their relation to two-dimensional quantum gravity such as Jackiw-Teitelboim and Liouville theory.

subtopics.name: Renormalization group fixed points and critical exponents
subtopics.scope: Perturbative and non-perturbative renormalization group analysis of scalar, Yukawa and gauge field theories, their fixed points, beta functions and critical exponents.

subtopics.name: Extra dimensions and Kaluza-Klein theories
subtopics.scope: Models with flat or warped extra dimensions, their Kaluza-Klein spectra, brane-localized fields, radion stabilization and low-energy phenomenology.

subtopics.name: Finite-volume methods for hadron interactions
subtopics.scope: Relating finite-volume energy levels and matrix elements computed in lattice QCD to infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, resonance parameters and decay rates.

subtopics.name: Lattice fermions and chiral symmetry
subtopics.scope: Wilson, staggered, domain-wall and overlap discretizations of fermions on the lattice, and their doublers, chiral symmetry, index theorems and Dirac spectra.

subtopics.name: Hamiltonian and strong-coupling lattice gauge theory
subtopics.scope: Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian formulations, strong-coupling expansions, quantum link models and low-dimensional lattice gauge theories studied with tensor networks or quantum simulation.

subtopics.name: Soft-collinear effective theory and resummation
subtopics.scope: Factorization theorems and all-order resummation of large logarithms in collider observables such as event shapes, jet rates, threshold and transverse-momentum spectra.

subtopics.name: Parton evolution and small-x QCD
subtopics.scope: Scale and energy evolution of parton distributions and high-energy scattering via DGLAP, BFKL and non-linear saturation equations.

subtopics.name: Heavy quarkonium and nonrelativistic effective theories
subtopics.scope: Spectra, decays and production of heavy-quark bound states and heavy hadrons using NRQCD, pNRQCD, heavy quark effective theory and potential models.

subtopics.name: Chiral perturbation theory and low-energy hadrons
subtopics.scope: Low-energy dynamics of pions, kaons and nucleons from chiral effective Lagrangians, unitarization and dispersive methods.

subtopics.name: Flavor physics and rare meson decays
subtopics.scope: Quark flavor transitions, CKM structure, neutral meson mixing and loop-induced or rare decays of K, D and B mesons in the Standard Model and beyond.

subtopics.name: Neutrino masses, mixing and oscillations
subtopics.scope: Origin of neutrino masses in seesaw and radiative models, lepton mixing from flavor symmetries, and neutrino oscillation phenomenology in vacuum and matter.

subtopics.name: Dark matter production and detection
subtopics.scope: Particle dark matter models, their relic abundance through freeze-out or freeze-in, and the resulting direct, indirect and collider detection rates.

subtopics.name: Baryogenesis and leptogenesis
subtopics.scope: Dynamical generation of the cosmic baryon asymmetry through out-of-equilibrium CP- and baryon-number-violating processes such as sphaleron transitions and heavy-neutrino decays.

subtopics.name: Axions and axion-like particles
subtopics.scope: The strong CP problem, QCD axion and axion-like particle models, their potentials, couplings, cosmological production and detection signatures.

subtopics.name: Extended Higgs sectors and vacuum stability
subtopics.scope: Singlet, doublet and triplet scalar extensions of the Standard Model, their spectra, couplings, unitarity and boundedness constraints, and the stability of the electroweak vacuum.

subtopics.name: Grand unification and proton decay
subtopics.scope: Unified gauge groups such as SU(5), SO(10) and E6, gauge coupling unification, symmetry-breaking chains, fermion mass relations and baryon-number-violating decays.

subtopics.name: Standard Model effective field theory
subtopics.scope: Parametrizing heavy new physics by higher-dimensional operators in SMEFT and low-energy EFT, including operator bases, matching, renormalization-group running and precision constraints.

subtopics.name: Precision QED and anomalous magnetic moments
subtopics.scope: Higher-order QED and electroweak radiative corrections to lepton magnetic moments, bound-state energy levels, and hadronic vacuum-polarization and light-by-light contributions.

subtopics.name: Thermal field theory and quark-gluon plasma
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium and near-equilibrium properties of hot gauge theories, including thermodynamics, screening, transport coefficients and particle production rates in the quark-gluon plasma.

subtopics.name: Cosmological first-order phase transitions
subtopics.scope: Thermal effective potentials, bubble nucleation, wall dynamics and the stochastic gravitational-wave spectra produced by first-order phase transitions in the early universe.

subtopics.name: Inflationary cosmology and primordial perturbations
subtopics.scope: Inflaton dynamics and model building, and the computation of scalar and tensor power spectra, spectral tilts and non-Gaussianities of primordial fluctuations.

subtopics.name: Modified gravity and cosmological dynamics
subtopics.scope: Extensions of general relativity such as f(R), scalar-tensor, Horndeski, massive and teleparallel gravity, and their cosmological background and perturbation dynamics.

subtopics.name: Exact solutions of Einstein's equations
subtopics.scope: Construction and classification of exact solutions of general relativity and Einstein-matter systems, including black holes, wormholes, gravitational waves and inhomogeneous cosmologies.

subtopics.name: Black hole perturbations and quasinormal modes
subtopics.scope: Linear perturbations of black holes and compact objects, including quasinormal-mode spectra, greybody factors, tidal Love numbers, superradiance and stability.

subtopics.name: Post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian binary dynamics
subtopics.scope: Analytic approximations to the conservative and dissipative dynamics of gravitationally bound binaries, including Hamiltonians, radiated fluxes, self-force and effective-one-body mappings.

subtopics.name: Quantum fields in curved spacetime
subtopics.scope: Quantization of fields on curved or time-dependent backgrounds, including Hawking and Unruh effects, cosmological particle creation, renormalized stress tensors and Casimir energies.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

subtopics.name: Loop quantum gravity and quantum cosmology
subtopics.scope: Canonical and covariant non-perturbative quantization of gravity with spin networks and spin foams, and loop or Wheeler-DeWitt quantum cosmology.

subtopics.name: Geodesics, black hole shadows and lensing
subtopics.scope: Motion of test particles and light in stationary spacetimes, including photon spheres, shadows, gravitational lensing angles and circular-orbit properties.

subtopics.name: Relativistic stars and compact objects
subtopics.scope: Structure, stability and tidal properties of neutron stars, boson stars and other self-gravitating compact objects in general relativity and alternative theories.

subtopics.name: Black hole thermodynamics and information
subtopics.scope: Thermodynamics of black holes across gravitational theories, microstate counting, and the information problem including Page curves and islands.

techniques.name: Feynman integrals in dimensional regularization
techniques.scope: Evaluating loop integrals with Feynman or Schwinger parameters, Mellin-Barnes representations, integration-by-parts reduction to master integrals and canonical differential equations, giving Laurent expansions in epsilon with polylogarithmic coefficients.

techniques.name: Renormalization and anomalous dimension computation
techniques.scope: Extracting counterterms, beta functions and anomalous dimensions at one or more loops and solving the resulting renormalization-group equations for running couplings, fixed points and critical exponents.

techniques.name: EFT matching and expansion by regions
techniques.scope: Integrating out heavy degrees of freedom by matching amplitudes or Green's functions at threshold, organized by power counting and the method of regions, to obtain Wilson coefficients and their scale dependence.

techniques.name: On-shell recursion and unitarity cuts
techniques.scope: Constructing tree and loop amplitudes from factorization and unitarity with spinor-helicity variables, BCFW recursion and generalized cuts projected onto a basis of integrals.

techniques.name: Dispersion relations and sum rules
techniques.scope: Using analyticity, crossing and unitarity to write dispersive representations and sum rules that fix low-energy constants, bound EFT couplings or relate spectral functions to observables.

techniques.name: Conformal block decomposition and inversion
techniques.scope: Expanding correlators in conformal blocks and using crossing, lightcone limits and the Lorentzian inversion formula to extract operator dimensions and OPE coefficients analytically.

techniques.name: Large-N saddle-point expansions
techniques.scope: Introducing auxiliary fields or eigenvalue densities, solving the saddle-point equations, and computing 1/N corrections from fluctuation determinants in vector, matrix and disordered models.

techniques.name: Instanton and bounce semiclassics
techniques.scope: Finding Euclidean classical solutions and computing their actions, zero modes and fluctuation determinants (for example with the Gel'fand-Yaglom method) to obtain tunneling rates and non-perturbative contributions.

techniques.name: Heat-kernel and zeta-function regularization
techniques.scope: Computing one-loop effective actions, Casimir energies, trace anomalies and functional determinants from Seeley-DeWitt coefficients and spectral zeta functions.

techniques.name: Bethe ansatz and integrable bootstrap
techniques.scope: Solving integrable models with the coordinate or algebraic Bethe ansatz, Yang-Baxter-consistent S-matrices and the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz to obtain exact spectra and free energies.

techniques.name: Supersymmetric localization and index counting
techniques.scope: Reducing supersymmetric path integrals and indices to finite-dimensional matrix or contour integrals over BPS loci, then evaluating them with residues, plethystic formulas or asymptotic expansions.

techniques.name: Group theory and anomaly cancellation
techniques.scope: Decomposing representations with branching rules, characters and Hilbert series, and imposing gauge and gravitational anomaly cancellation or matching conditions to constrain spectra and charges.

techniques.name: Holographic bulk solutions and renormalized actions
techniques.scope: Solving bulk field equations in asymptotically AdS backgrounds with the appropriate boundary conditions, then evaluating holographically renormalized on-shell actions, extremal surfaces or fluctuation spectra.

techniques.name: Bogoliubov transformations and mode quantization
techniques.scope: Solving mode equations on curved or time-dependent backgrounds and relating in and out vacua through Bogoliubov coefficients to obtain particle production, spectra and effective temperatures.

techniques.name: Black hole perturbation spectral methods
techniques.scope: Reducing linear perturbations to master radial equations and computing quasinormal frequencies, greybody factors and Love numbers with WKB, Frobenius or continued-fraction expansions, or matched hypergeometric solutions.

techniques.name: Effective potential and thermal resummation
techniques.scope: Computing Coleman-Weinberg and finite-temperature effective potentials with Matsubara sums, daisy resummation and high-temperature expansions to find minima, critical temperatures and transition strengths.

techniques.name: Boltzmann equations for cosmological relics
techniques.scope: Setting up and solving, analytically or semi-numerically, Boltzmann equations with thermally averaged rates to obtain freeze-out or freeze-in abundances, asymmetries and washout factors.

techniques.name: Cosmological perturbation theory and slow-roll
techniques.scope: Deriving gauge-invariant perturbation equations on FRW backgrounds and solving them in slow-roll or de Sitter approximations to obtain power spectra, spectral tilts and non-Gaussianity parameters.

techniques.name: Post-Newtonian and worldline EFT expansions
techniques.scope: Expanding the dynamics of gravitating bodies in v/c or G using point-particle worldline actions, separation into potential and radiation modes, and multipole radiation formulas to obtain Hamiltonians and fluxes.

techniques.name: Lattice momentum-space and finite-volume analysis
techniques.scope: Analyzing lattice actions in Brillouin-zone momentum space for dispersion relations, doublers and lattice perturbation theory, and deriving finite-volume quantization conditions and lattice sums.

subtopics.name: Quantum channel capacities and additivity
subtopics.scope: Classical, quantum, private and entanglement-assisted capacities of noisy quantum channels, including degradability, superadditivity and single-letter formulas.

subtopics.name: Quantum entropies and divergence inequalities
subtopics.scope: Properties of von Neumann, Rényi, and smooth min/max entropies and relative entropies, including continuity bounds, uncertainty relations and one-shot quantities.

subtopics.name: Quantum hypothesis testing and state discrimination
subtopics.scope: Optimal measurements and error probabilities for distinguishing quantum states or channels, from single-shot Helstrom bounds to asymptotic Chernoff and Stein exponents.

subtopics.name: Structure and characterization of quantum channels
subtopics.scope: Mathematical properties of completely positive maps, such as Choi-Kraus representations, extremality, divisibility, covariance, and positivity versus complete positivity.

subtopics.name: Entanglement detection and quantification
subtopics.scope: Separability criteria, entanglement witnesses and computable entanglement measures for bipartite and multipartite mixed states.

subtopics.name: LOCC entanglement manipulation and majorization
subtopics.scope: Convertibility, distillation, dilution and catalysis of entangled states under local operations and classical communication.

subtopics.name: Bell nonlocality, steering, and nonlocal games
subtopics.scope: Correlations that violate local-hidden-variable or local-hidden-state models, their quantum bounds, nonlocal games and measurement incompatibility.

subtopics.name: Contextuality, ontological models and generalized probabilistic theories
subtopics.scope: Foundational structure of quantum theory beyond Bell scenarios, including Kochen-Specker and generalized (Spekkens) contextuality, noncontextuality inequalities and their graph-theoretic and sheaf-theoretic characterizations, ontological models and psi-ontic versus psi-epistemic theorems, Leggett-Garg macrorealism tests, and generalized probabilistic theories with operational reconstructions of quantum theory.

subtopics.name: Mutually unbiased bases and SIC-POVMs
subtopics.scope: Construction, existence and properties of mutually unbiased bases, symmetric informationally complete measurements and related designs in finite dimensions.

subtopics.name: Haar-random states, unitaries and designs
subtopics.scope: Typical properties of Haar-random states and unitaries, and how random circuits converge to unitary t-designs.

subtopics.name: Stabilizer codes and quantum code bounds
subtopics.scope: Construction of stabilizer, CSS and LDPC quantum codes, their parameters, and fundamental bounds on rate and distance.

subtopics.name: Topological codes and fault-tolerance thresholds
subtopics.scope: Surface, toric and color codes, their decoders, and error thresholds under various noise models.

subtopics.name: Bosonic codes in oscillator modes
subtopics.scope: Encoding qubits in harmonic oscillators with GKP, cat, binomial and rotation-symmetric codes, and how these codes perform under loss and dephasing.

subtopics.name: Magic state distillation and fault-tolerant gadgets
subtopics.scope: Protocols for universal fault-tolerant computation, including magic state distillation, code switching, and estimates of overheads and thresholds.

subtopics.name: Dynamical decoupling and noise filtering
subtopics.scope: Pulse sequences that suppress decoherence, and the filter-function description of qubits subject to classical or quantum noise spectra.

subtopics.name: Randomized benchmarking and noise characterization
subtopics.scope: Estimating average gate fidelities, error rates and noise models of quantum devices with randomized protocols and process tomography.

subtopics.name: Quantum query algorithms and complexity
subtopics.scope: Query-model algorithms such as search, period finding and hidden subgroup problems, and lower bounds on their query complexity.

subtopics.name: Hamiltonian simulation and quantum signal processing
subtopics.scope: Algorithms that implement time evolution or matrix functions on quantum computers, including product formulas, LCU, qubitization and QSVT.

subtopics.name: Quantum walks and coherent transport on networks
subtopics.scope: Quantum walks and coherent excitation transport on graphs, lattices and spin networks, including discrete- and continuous-time walk dynamics, spreading and localization, walk-based search, universal computation and graph-property testing, topological phases of walks, decoherence- and environment-assisted transport, and high-fidelity state transfer and routing through spin chains and engineered couplings.
subtopics.broadened_from: Quantum walks on graphs and state transfer

subtopics.name: Adiabatic quantum computation and annealing
subtopics.scope: Computation by slow Hamiltonian interpolation, focusing on spectral gaps, diabatic errors and annealing schedules for optimization problems.

subtopics.name: QAOA and variational quantum algorithms
subtopics.scope: Parameterized quantum circuits optimized by a classical loop, including QAOA performance guarantees, variational eigensolvers and trainability issues.

subtopics.name: Quantum complexity classes and Hamiltonian complexity
subtopics.scope: Structural quantum complexity theory beyond query models, covering quantum complexity classes and their relations (BQP, QMA, QCMA, QMA(2), QIP, PostBQP), quantum interactive and Merlin-Arthur proof systems, verification of quantum computation, and the computational hardness of physical problems such as local Hamiltonian ground energies, stoquastic and sign-problem-free Hamiltonians, the quantum PCP conjecture, circuit-to-Hamiltonian and perturbative-gadget reductions, and universal analog Hamiltonian simulators.
subtopics.broadened_from: Quantum Hamiltonian complexity and local Hamiltonians

subtopics.name: Classical simulation of restricted quantum circuits
subtopics.scope: Efficient or near-efficient classical algorithms for Clifford, matchgate, low-magic, low-entanglement and noisy circuits, and the resources that make simulation hard.

subtopics.name: Quantum gate synthesis and circuit compilation
subtopics.scope: Decomposing unitaries into gate sets, minimizing gate counts and depth, and the structure of Clifford and Clifford+T circuits.

subtopics.name: Measurement-based computation and graph states
subtopics.scope: One-way quantum computing on cluster and graph states, and the entanglement structure, local equivalence and resource properties of those states.

subtopics.name: Quantum key distribution security and rates
subtopics.scope: Security proofs and achievable secret key rates for discrete- and continuous-variable QKD protocols with realistic imperfections.

subtopics.name: Quantum two-party cryptography and coin flipping
subtopics.scope: Cryptographic primitives between parties who distrust each other, such as coin flipping, bit commitment, oblivious transfer and position verification, with their optimal biases and impossibility results.

subtopics.name: Quantum repeaters and entanglement distribution
subtopics.scope: Protocols for distributing entanglement over lossy links using swapping, purification and quantum memories, with analysis of their rates and fidelities.

subtopics.name: Optimal cloning and quantum state estimation
subtopics.scope: Fundamental limits on copying, broadcasting and estimating unknown quantum states from finitely many copies, including optimal covariant measurements and tomography.

subtopics.name: Quantum metrology and parameter estimation
subtopics.scope: Precision limits for estimating physical parameters with quantum probes, including Heisenberg scaling, the effects of noise, and multiparameter bounds.

subtopics.name: Open quantum systems and master equations
subtopics.scope: Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics of systems coupled to environments, including Lindblad, Redfield and exactly solvable spin-boson-type models.

subtopics.name: Continuous measurement and quantum feedback
subtopics.scope: Dynamics of continuously monitored quantum systems, described by stochastic master equations and quantum trajectories, and feedback control based on the measurement record.

subtopics.name: Quantum thermodynamics and work extraction
subtopics.scope: Work, heat and efficiency in quantum systems, including heat engines, batteries, fluctuation theorems and thermal operations.

subtopics.name: Resource theories of coherence and magic
subtopics.scope: Axiomatic quantification and conversion of resources such as coherence, asymmetry and non-stabilizerness under restricted sets of free operations.

subtopics.name: Gaussian continuous-variable quantum information
subtopics.scope: Quantum information with Gaussian states and operations of bosonic modes, including entanglement, channels and capacities in phase space.

subtopics.name: Photonic quantum information processing with linear optics
subtopics.scope: Discrete-variable photonic quantum information, covering multiphoton interference and the complexity of boson sampling, linear-optical and fusion-based quantum computing with heralded gates, photon sources, detectors and integrated multiport circuits, and how photon distinguishability and loss limit photonic protocols.
subtopics.broadened_from: Linear optics, interferometry and boson sampling

subtopics.name: Quantum information in many-body systems
subtopics.scope: Quantum-information views of interacting lattice and many-body systems: entanglement structure and area laws in ground and excited states, tensor-network representations and algorithms (MPS, PEPS, MERA), classification of gapped, symmetry-protected and topologically ordered phases by their entanglement, and how information spreads in many-body dynamics, including Lieb-Robinson bounds, entanglement growth after quenches, thermalization and many-body localization, scrambling, and measurement-induced entanglement transitions.

subtopics.name: Relativistic quantum information and field entanglement
subtopics.scope: Entanglement and quantum information in quantum fields and in curved or accelerated settings, including Unruh-DeWitt detectors and entanglement harvesting.

subtopics.name: Superconducting, trapped-ion and atomic qubit physics
subtopics.scope: Theoretical models of physical qubit platforms, including circuit QED, trapped-ion gates and Rydberg-atom arrays, and of their gate errors.

subtopics.name: Quantum speed limits and optimal control
subtopics.scope: Minimal evolution times and optimal control fields for preparing states and implementing gates under constraints.

techniques.name: Semidefinite programming and duality bounds
techniques.scope: Formulate optimal guessing probabilities, Bell values, fidelities or channel norms as SDPs and certify the exact optimum with matching primal and dual solutions.

techniques.name: Weingarten calculus for Haar averages
techniques.scope: Evaluate moments of Haar-random unitaries and states with Weingarten functions and permutation sums to get exact averages and variances.

techniques.name: Schur-Weyl duality and representation theory
techniques.scope: Decompose tensor-power spaces into irreducible representations of the unitary and symmetric groups, reducing symmetric problems to low-dimensional ones.

techniques.name: Binary symplectic stabilizer algebra
techniques.scope: Represent Pauli and Clifford operations as vectors and matrices over GF(2) to compute code parameters, logical operators and counts of stabilizer objects.

techniques.name: Discrete Fourier analysis and character sums
techniques.scope: Use Fourier transforms over finite groups and fields, Gauss sums and MacWilliams identities to construct bases, analyze algorithms and relate weight distributions.

techniques.name: Statistical-mechanics mapping of decoding thresholds
techniques.scope: Map optimal decoding of topological codes onto disordered spin models or percolation problems to locate error thresholds.

techniques.name: Symplectic and Bogoliubov mode transformations
techniques.scope: Diagonalize Gaussian covariance matrices and quadratic mode Hamiltonians with Williamson normal forms and Bogoliubov transformations to get entropies, entanglement and particle content.

techniques.name: Phase-space quasiprobability representations
techniques.scope: Use continuous or discrete Wigner, Husimi and characteristic functions to compute overlaps, negativity and channel actions in closed form.

techniques.name: Quantum Fisher information calculus
techniques.scope: Compute the symmetric-logarithmic-derivative QFI, Bures metrics and their extensions to channels to get exact precision bounds and optimal probe states.

techniques.name: Convex-roof and symmetry-reduced entanglement evaluation
techniques.scope: Use symmetries (twirling, Werner and isotropic families) and convex-roof constructions to get closed-form entanglement and resource measures.

techniques.name: Entropic inequalities and converse bounds
techniques.scope: Chain data-processing, subadditivity and continuity inequalities to derive tight converse bounds on rates and capacities.

techniques.name: Large-deviation and second-order asymptotics
techniques.scope: Derive error exponents, Chernoff and Hoeffding bounds, and Gaussian second-order corrections for asymptotic information-processing tasks.

techniques.name: Liouvillian spectral analysis of master equations
techniques.scope: Vectorize Lindblad generators and solve for their spectra, steady states and relaxation times, either exactly or by third quantization.

techniques.name: Free-fermion correlation-matrix methods
techniques.scope: Solve quadratic fermionic models with the Jordan-Wigner mapping and correlation matrices, using Toeplitz or Fisher-Hartwig asymptotics for entanglement.

techniques.name: Schrieffer-Wolff and perturbative effective Hamiltonians
techniques.scope: Derive low-energy effective couplings, dispersive shifts and gadget interactions by perturbative block diagonalization.

techniques.name: Spectral gap bounds and adiabatic theorems
techniques.scope: Bound or compute the gaps of Hamiltonians, graph Laplacians and Markov chains, and convert them into adiabatic run times, hitting times or mixing times.

techniques.name: BCH, Magnus and nested-commutator expansions
techniques.scope: Expand time-ordered or product-formula evolutions in commutators to get leading error terms, average Hamiltonians and filter functions.

techniques.name: Polynomial approximation and Chebyshev methods
techniques.scope: Use Chebyshev and minimax polynomial approximations to build quantum signal processing sequences and to prove polynomial-method query lower bounds.

techniques.name: Transfer matrices and tensor-network contraction
techniques.scope: Compute correlation lengths, norms and entanglement of MPS-like states, or classical partition functions, from transfer-matrix spectra.

techniques.name: Lie-algebraic and Cartan decomposition methods
techniques.scope: Use Lie algebra structure, Cartan (KAK) decompositions and dynamical Lie algebras to determine controllability, optimal gate times and invariants.

subtopics.name: Nuclear effective field theory and few-body systems
subtopics.scope: Pionless and chiral effective-field-theory descriptions of nuclear forces, applied to two-, three- and four-nucleon bound states, scattering and universal low-energy behavior.

subtopics.name: Shell model and exactly solvable models
subtopics.scope: Configuration-interaction descriptions of nuclei, and schematic solvable Hamiltonians (pairing, seniority, Lipkin-type) used to benchmark many-body approximations.

subtopics.name: Nuclear density functionals and mean-field theory
subtopics.scope: Skyrme, Gogny and relativistic mean-field energy density functionals for ground-state properties, deformation and giant resonances across the nuclear chart.

subtopics.name: Collective motion: geometric and algebraic models
subtopics.scope: Bohr-Mottelson geometric collective Hamiltonians, interacting boson models and dynamical symmetries describing vibrational, rotational and transitional nuclear spectra.

subtopics.name: Dense matter equation of state and neutron stars
subtopics.scope: The equation of state of nuclear and quark matter at high density, and what it implies for neutron-star structure, tidal deformability, cooling and superfluidity.

subtopics.name: Nuclear reaction and scattering theory
subtopics.scope: Optical-model, coupled-channels, R-matrix, eikonal and breakup descriptions of elastic, inelastic, transfer and fusion reactions.

subtopics.name: Radioactive decay, fission and barrier penetration
subtopics.scope: Alpha decay, cluster and proton emission, and fission treated as quantum tunneling through nuclear potential barriers, including half-life systematics.

subtopics.name: Thermonuclear reaction rates and nucleosynthesis
subtopics.scope: Theory of low-energy astrophysical reaction rates, plasma screening and network freeze-out, which underlie big-bang, stellar, s-process and r-process nucleosynthesis.

subtopics.name: Weak interactions and fundamental symmetries in nuclei
subtopics.scope: Beta decay, neutrinoless double-beta decay, neutrino-nucleus interactions, and symmetry-violating observables such as electric dipole moments in nuclear systems.

subtopics.name: Relativistic hydrodynamics of heavy-ion collisions
subtopics.scope: Ideal and viscous relativistic fluid dynamics, its kinetic-theory foundations and attractor behavior, applied to the expanding quark-gluon plasma.

subtopics.name: Hard probes and heavy quarks in QGP
subtopics.scope: Jet energy loss, heavy-quark diffusion and quarkonium dissociation as probes of the hot medium created in nuclear collisions.

subtopics.name: QCD phase diagram and chiral transition
subtopics.scope: Effective-model and field-theory studies of the chiral and deconfinement transitions, the critical point, and color superconductivity at finite temperature and density.

subtopics.name: Hadron spectroscopy and exotic hadrons
subtopics.scope: Quark-model, heavy-quark-symmetry and hadronic-molecule descriptions of meson and baryon spectra, including tetraquark and pentaquark candidates.

subtopics.name: Partonic structure of nucleons and nuclei
subtopics.scope: Parton distributions, form factors, generalized and transverse-momentum-dependent distributions, nuclear modifications and small-x saturation.

techniques.name: EFT matching, power counting and loops
techniques.scope: Build effective Lagrangians, order contributions by power counting, and evaluate loop integrals in dimensional regularization to get amplitudes, low-energy constants or corrections at a fixed order.

techniques.name: Renormalization group flow and fixed points
techniques.scope: Derive and solve Wilsonian, functional or similarity renormalization-group equations for couplings to find fixed points, critical exponents, running behavior or limit cycles.

techniques.name: Effective-range expansion and partial-wave analysis
techniques.scope: Decompose scattering amplitudes into partial waves and extract phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, pole positions or finite-volume energy shifts.

techniques.name: Self-consistent mean field and BCS
techniques.scope: Use variational Hartree-Fock and BCS/Bogoliubov treatments to obtain gap equations, self-consistency conditions, and closed-form energies or critical values.

techniques.name: Random phase approximation and linear response
techniques.scope: Linearize the equations of motion around a ground state to compute collective excitation energies, strength functions, energy-weighted sum rules or response functions.

techniques.name: Group theory and angular-momentum algebra
techniques.scope: Use Lie-algebra Casimirs, dynamical symmetries, and Clebsch-Gordan and Racah recoupling to get spectra, selection rules and transition ratios exactly.

techniques.name: WKB and semiclassical barrier penetration
techniques.scope: Use semiclassical quantization and tunneling integrals to obtain penetrabilities, half-lives, Gamow factors and Bohr-Sommerfeld spectra.

techniques.name: Hyperspherical and Faddeev three-body methods
techniques.scope: Reduce three-body problems in hyperspherical coordinates, or through Faddeev equations, to transcendental equations for scaling exponents, bound-state energies or recombination rates.

techniques.name: Finite-temperature field theory and resummation
techniques.scope: Use Matsubara sums, hard-thermal-loop resummation and thermal self-energies to compute screening masses, damping rates, pressures and the correlators behind transport coefficients.

techniques.name: Kinetic theory and analytic hydrodynamic solutions
techniques.scope: Solve Boltzmann equations in the relaxation-time approximation or in moment expansions, and construct symmetric flow solutions, to derive transport coefficients, attractors and relaxation rates.

techniques.name: Dispersion relations and sum rules
techniques.scope: Use analyticity, unitarity and the operator product expansion to derive dispersive representations, sum rules and bounds on spectral quantities.

techniques.name: Factorization and QCD evolution equations
techniques.scope: Apply collinear, TMD or small-x factorization with DGLAP, BFKL or BK evolution, Mellin moments and anomalous dimensions to obtain scaling laws and asymptotic forms.

subtopics.name: Frustrated magnets and quantum spin liquids
subtopics.scope: Spin systems frustrated by geometry or competing exchange (triangular, kagome, pyrochlore, J1-J2 lattices) and their spin-liquid, valence-bond and order-by-disorder phases.

subtopics.name: Spin-orbital physics of correlated insulators
subtopics.scope: Magnetism and orbital physics of Mott and charge-transfer insulators where orbital degrees of freedom or strong spin-orbit coupling shape the exchange, including Kugel-Khomskii, compass and orbital-ordering models, cooperative Jahn-Teller effects, j_eff=1/2 pseudospins and Kitaev-Heisenberg-Gamma bond-dependent exchange in 3d/4d/5d materials, exactly solvable Kitaev-type models, multipolar and quadrupolar order in d- and f-electron compounds, and excitonic Van Vleck magnetism of d4 ions.

subtopics.name: Hubbard models and the Mott transition
subtopics.scope: Lattice models of strongly correlated electrons and the metal-insulator transition driven by interactions, including the t-J limit, magnetism and doped Mott insulators.

subtopics.name: Heavy fermions and Kondo lattices
subtopics.scope: Lattices of localized f-moments coupled to conduction electrons, covering hybridization, the competition between Kondo screening and RKKY coupling, and the formation of a heavy Fermi liquid.

subtopics.name: Quantum impurity models and Kondo effect
subtopics.scope: One or a few magnetic impurities or quantum dots coupled to fermionic or bosonic baths, including multichannel, pseudogap and Bose-Fermi Kondo problems.

subtopics.name: One-dimensional and quasi-one-dimensional quantum matter
subtopics.scope: Field-theoretic and numerical study of interacting electrons, spins and bosons in one and quasi-one dimensions, including quantum wires, nanotubes, spin chains, spin ladders and coupled-chain materials, using bosonization, conformal field theory, renormalization group and DMRG to describe Luttinger-liquid and gapped phases, impurities and boundaries, spin-charge separation, and the crossover from one dimension to higher dimensions in coupled chains.

subtopics.name: Integrable models and Bethe ansatz
subtopics.scope: Exactly solvable one-dimensional quantum many-body models (XXZ chains, Lieb-Liniger and Yang-Gaudin gases, the Hubbard chain) and their spectra, thermodynamics and correlations.

subtopics.name: Quantum criticality and non-Fermi liquids
subtopics.scope: Metals near quantum phase transitions, and related solvable models such as Hertz-Millis, Ising-nematic and SYK, in which quasiparticles break down.

subtopics.name: Interacting electrons in Landau levels and Chern bands
subtopics.scope: Many-body phases of strongly interacting electrons in quantum Hall Landau levels and topological Chern bands: fractional quantum Hall and fractional Chern insulator states, composite fermions and Chern-Simons field theories, quantum Hall ferromagnets and charged skyrmions, bilayer exciton condensates, Wigner crystals and stripe or bubble phases, plus their anyonic excitations, collective modes and edge transport.

subtopics.name: Spin-wave theory of ordered magnets
subtopics.scope: Magnon excitations, thermodynamics and quantum corrections in ferromagnets, antiferromagnets and noncollinear magnets with long-range order.

subtopics.name: Topological order, anyons, and emergent gauge fields
subtopics.scope: Long-range-entangled phases and the gauge-theoretic and categorical frameworks that describe them, including lattice and Chern-Simons gauge theories, anyon braiding and modular tensor categories, string-net, toric-code and fracton models, generalized higher-form and non-invertible symmetries and their anomalies, field-theory dualities and confinement or deconfinement transitions, and topological quantum codes and fault-tolerant topological quantum computation.
subtopics.broadened_from: Topological order and emergent gauge theories

subtopics.name: Generalized symmetries, anomalies, and interacting topological phases
subtopics.scope: Non-perturbative constraints that global, higher-form, subsystem and non-invertible symmetries place on interacting quantum many-body systems: bosonic and fermionic symmetry-protected topological phases (such as the Haldane chain), their group-cohomology and cobordism classification, how interactions reduce free-fermion classifications, 't Hooft anomaly matching and Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorems, gapless and intrinsically gapless SPTs, symmetry-protected edge modes, and lattice and tensor-network realizations.

subtopics.name: Charge and spin density waves
