subtopics.scope: Instabilities of metals toward periodic charge or spin modulation driven by nesting, electron-phonon coupling or interactions, including Peierls physics and sliding dynamics.

subtopics.name: Interacting electron gas and Fermi liquids
subtopics.scope: Homogeneous interacting electron systems treated with Landau Fermi-liquid theory and RPA, covering screening, plasmons, collective modes and quasiparticle lifetimes.

subtopics.name: Band topology, Wannier functions, and crystalline symmetry
subtopics.scope: Single-particle band theory of crystalline solids and metamaterials and its geometric and topological structure: space-group and magnetic-group band representations, symmetry indicators and topological quantum chemistry, Wannier functions and obstructed atomic limits, Berry-phase theory of polarization and orbital magnetization, tenfold-way classification of gapped insulators and superconductors (Chern, Z2, crystalline and higher-order phases, fragile topology), and their boundary and defect states, including in topological phononic, photonic and mechanical lattices.
subtopics.broadened_from: Topological band insulators and crystalline topology

subtopics.name: Weyl and Dirac semimetals
subtopics.scope: Gapless band structures with protected point or line degeneracies, and their surface arcs, anomalies and electromagnetic responses.

subtopics.name: Two-dimensional crystals and valley physics
subtopics.scope: Electronic, transport and electromechanical properties of atomically thin crystals and non-moiré van der Waals stacks, including graphene and its multilayers, transition-metal dichalcogenides, phosphorene, hexagonal boron nitride and Xenes, covering massless and massive Dirac low-energy theories, valley and layer pseudospins, gate-tunable band gaps, strain-induced pseudo-gauge fields, Klein tunneling, dielectric screening and 2D plasmons.

subtopics.name: Flat-band materials and quantum geometry
subtopics.scope: Electronic systems whose kinetic energy is quenched by lattice geometry, moiré superlattices, or band engineering, including twisted and lattice-mismatched van der Waals stacks, rhombohedral multilayer graphene, kagome, Lieb and other line-graph lattices, and artificial superlattices, studied for how flat bands form, their quantum metric and band geometry, and the flat-band ferromagnetism, superconductivity, and correlated insulating states they host.

subtopics.name: Scattering theory of mesoscopic transport
subtopics.scope: Phase-coherent conduction through nanostructures described by transmission eigenvalues, including conductance, shot noise, thermoelectric response and full counting statistics.

subtopics.name: Quantum dots and Coulomb blockade
subtopics.scope: Confined few-electron systems and single-electron devices governed by charging energy, level spacing and tunneling.

subtopics.name: Integer quantum Hall effect and edge states
subtopics.scope: Noninteracting two-dimensional electrons in strong magnetic fields, including Landau-level structure, chiral edge channels, Hofstadter spectra and plateau transitions.

subtopics.name: Spin-orbit coupling and spin transport
subtopics.scope: Generation, transport and relaxation of spin in metals and semiconductors through spin-orbit coupling, including spin Hall effects, spin pumping and spin torques.

subtopics.name: Linear and nonlinear response of Bloch quasiparticles
subtopics.scope: Kubo-formula and semiclassical Boltzmann/wave-packet theories of how crystalline electrons and other band quasiparticles respond to electric, magnetic, thermal and optical fields, including anomalous and nonlinear Hall effects, thermoelectric and thermal Hall transport (also of magnons and phonons), orbital magnetization and magnetoelectric coupling, magneto-optical Kerr/Faraday rotation, and second-order optical responses such as shift and injection currents and second-harmonic generation.

subtopics.name: Floquet engineering of periodically driven systems
subtopics.scope: Periodically driven quantum systems whose effective Hamiltonians, quasienergy spectra and anomalous topological phases differ from static ones.

subtopics.name: Non-Hermitian band theory and skin effect
subtopics.scope: Effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians for gain, loss or nonreciprocity, including exceptional points, generalized Brillouin zones and the skin effect.

subtopics.name: Topological superconductors and superconducting hybrid heterostructures
subtopics.scope: Classification, model building and material realization of superconducting phases with protected boundary or defect modes, including Majorana and parafermion zero modes, chiral and helical edge states, higher-order and crystalline topological superconductors, Yu-Shiba-Rusinov impurity bands, pairing induced by proximity in semiconductor, topological-insulator and magnetic hybrids, and braiding, fusion and topological-qubit proposals built on them.

subtopics.name: Dissipative and open quantum systems
subtopics.scope: Quantum systems coupled to environments, including spin-boson physics, Lindblad dynamics and nonequilibrium steady states of driven-dissipative many-body systems.

subtopics.name: Quantum oscillations and magnetotransport
subtopics.scope: Thermodynamic and transport phenomena in metals that depend on magnetic field, including de Haas-van Alphen and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations and classical magnetoresistance.

subtopics.name: Unconventional pairing symmetry and gap structure
subtopics.scope: Superconductors whose order parameters are not s-wave or change sign (d-wave, p-wave, s±, multiband), and their thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures.

subtopics.name: Vortex matter and Ginzburg-Landau theory
subtopics.scope: Mixed-state physics of type-II superconductors, from Ginzburg-Landau theory of vortices and critical fields to vortex lattices, pinning, mesoscopic samples and dynamics.

subtopics.name: Phonon-mediated and Eliashberg superconductivity
subtopics.scope: Conventional electron-phonon superconductivity treated with BCS and Migdal-Eliashberg theory, including Tc formulas, isotope effects and strong-coupling corrections.

subtopics.name: Andreev physics and Josephson junctions
subtopics.scope: Superconducting hybrids with normal metals, ferromagnets or semiconductors, covering Andreev reflection, the proximity effect and Josephson current-phase relations.

subtopics.name: Superconducting fluctuations and thin films
subtopics.scope: Thermal and quantum fluctuations of the superconducting order in low dimensions, including paraconductivity, BKT transitions, phase slips and superconductor-insulator transitions.

subtopics.name: Weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates
subtopics.scope: Dilute Bose gases at the Gross-Pitaevskii and Bogoliubov level, including collective modes, solitons, vortices and beyond-mean-field corrections.

subtopics.name: BCS-BEC crossover and unitary Fermi gases
subtopics.scope: Two-component Fermi gases with attraction tuned across a Feshbach resonance, including universality, contact relations, polarons and imbalanced pairing.

subtopics.name: Bose-Hubbard models and optical lattices
subtopics.scope: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices described by Bose- and Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonians, including superfluid-Mott transitions, trap effects and engineered lattice geometries.

subtopics.name: Spinor and spin-orbit-coupled quantum gases
subtopics.scope: Multicomponent atomic condensates with internal spin, synthetic gauge fields or Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling, and their unusual ground states.

subtopics.name: Dipolar quantum gases and supersolids
subtopics.scope: Ultracold gases with long-range anisotropic dipolar interactions, including roton softening, self-bound droplets and supersolid phases.

subtopics.name: Few-body physics and Efimov states
subtopics.scope: Problems of two, three or a few particles with short-range interactions, including universal bound states, Efimov physics and scattering in reduced dimensions.

subtopics.name: Quench dynamics and relaxation in isolated systems
subtopics.scope: Nonequilibrium evolution of closed many-body systems after sudden parameter changes, including thermalization, generalized Gibbs ensembles and light-cone spreading.

subtopics.name: Lattice vibrations, heat transport, and thermoelectricity
subtopics.scope: Phonon spectra, anharmonicity, soft modes and vibrational thermodynamics of crystals and amorphous solids, together with phonon and electronic heat conduction (diffusive, ballistic, hydrodynamic, interfacial and thermal-Hall) and thermoelectric effects in bulk, low-dimensional and nanostructured materials.

subtopics.name: Polarons and electron-phonon coupling
subtopics.scope: Charge carriers dressed by lattice distortions, from Fröhlich and Holstein polarons to bipolarons, and electron-phonon effects on band and transport properties.

subtopics.name: Symmetry-breaking phase transitions and classical criticality
subtopics.scope: Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson and renormalization-group theory of thermal symmetry-breaking transitions in solids and classical lattice models, covering ferroelectric, ferroelastic, multiferroic and soft-mode structural transitions, domains and order-parameter couplings, first-order and tricritical behavior, and the universality, scaling and critical exponents of classical statistical models.

subtopics.name: Mechanics and defects of crystalline and amorphous solids
subtopics.scope: Continuum and atomistic theory of how crystalline and amorphous solids deform, covering elastic moduli and anisotropic elasticity, point, line and planar defects and how they interact, dislocation-mediated plasticity and work hardening, fracture and friction, defect-mediated melting in two dimensions, and the yielding and shear-transformation plasticity of glasses.

subtopics.name: Micromagnetics, domain walls, and skyrmions
subtopics.scope: Continuum magnetization dynamics in ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, including domain walls, vortices, skyrmions and their motion driven by fields or currents.

subtopics.name: Excitons and optical response of semiconductors
subtopics.scope: Bound electron-hole pairs and light-matter coupling in bulk, quantum-well and two-dimensional semiconductors, including trions and exciton-polaritons.

subtopics.name: Spin glasses and replica theory
subtopics.scope: Disordered magnets and mean-field glassy systems, including the SK and p-spin models, replica symmetry breaking and glassy dynamics.

subtopics.name: Anderson localization and disordered conductors
subtopics.scope: Localization of single particles by disorder or quasiperiodicity, from weak-localization corrections to mobility edges and the Anderson transition.

subtopics.name: Ergodicity breaking, quantum circuits, and many-body hydrodynamics
subtopics.scope: Nonequilibrium phases and late-time dynamics of interacting quantum lattice systems, covering both failures of thermalization (many-body localization, quantum many-body scars, Hilbert-space fragmentation, kinetically constrained and Rydberg-blockade models, discrete time crystals and prethermal phases) and the universal ways ergodic systems spread information and conserved charges (random unitary and monitored circuits with measurement-induced transitions, operator spreading, and emergent diffusive, anomalous or KPZ hydrodynamics in quantum spin chains).

subtopics.name: Random matrix theory and quantum chaos
subtopics.scope: Spectral and eigenvector statistics of chaotic quantum systems and random Hamiltonians, including level spacings, spectral form factors and operator growth.

subtopics.name: Statistical mechanics of learning and neural networks
subtopics.scope: Analysis of neural networks, high-dimensional inference and associative memories with the tools of disordered-systems physics.

subtopics.name: Percolation and random networks
subtopics.scope: Geometric connectivity transitions on lattices and random graphs, including percolation thresholds, cluster statistics and network robustness.

subtopics.name: Disorder-driven criticality and strong-disorder RG
subtopics.scope: How quenched randomness changes phase transitions, including the Harris and Imry-Ma criteria, random-field models, infinite-randomness fixed points and Griffiths phases.

subtopics.name: Superfluid helium and quantum fluids
subtopics.scope: Superfluidity in helium-4, helium-3 and related quantum liquids, including two-fluid hydrodynamics, quantized vortices, quantum turbulence and the superfluid phases of helium-3.

subtopics.name: Entanglement in quantum many-body systems
subtopics.scope: Quantitative characterization of entanglement in ground and excited states, including area laws, logarithmic scaling at criticality and entanglement spectra.

techniques.name: Bethe ansatz and integrability methods
techniques.scope: Solve one-dimensional or impurity models exactly with coordinate or algebraic Bethe ansatz, Yang-Baxter structures or the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz to obtain energies, excitation spectra and thermodynamics.

techniques.name: Bosonization and refermionization
techniques.scope: Map interacting one-dimensional fermions or spins to free bosonic fields (or back to free fermions at special points) to compute scaling exponents, Luttinger parameters and correlation functions.

techniques.name: Renormalization-group flows and fixed points
techniques.scope: Derive beta functions by momentum-shell integration, epsilon expansion, real-space decimation or strong-disorder rules, and extract fixed points, critical exponents and crossover scales.

techniques.name: Large-N and saddle-point expansions
techniques.scope: Extend the number of flavors or the symmetry group to N, then solve the saddle point and its 1/N corrections to obtain phase boundaries, gaps and anomalous dimensions.

techniques.name: Self-consistent mean-field and gap equations
techniques.scope: Decouple interactions with Hartree-Fock, BCS or Hubbard-Stratonovich mean fields and solve the self-consistency equations for gaps, critical temperatures and phase diagrams.

techniques.name: Many-body Green's functions and diagrammatics
techniques.scope: Compute self-energies, susceptibilities and vertex corrections with Matsubara or real-time perturbation theory, RPA and ladder resummations.

techniques.name: Kubo linear-response calculations
techniques.scope: Evaluate correlation-function expressions for conductivities, Hall responses and susceptibilities, including Berry-curvature (TKNN) forms and sum rules.

techniques.name: Semiclassical Boltzmann and wave-packet dynamics
techniques.scope: Solve the Boltzmann transport equation in relaxation-time or exact form, and use wave-packet equations with Berry phases and Onsager quantization, to obtain transport and quantum-oscillation coefficients.

techniques.name: Scattering-matrix and Landauer-Büttiker methods
techniques.scope: Construct the transmission matrices of mesoscopic devices to obtain conductance, noise, counting statistics and thermoelectric coefficients.

techniques.name: Scattering phase shifts and T-matrix
techniques.scope: Solve two-body or impurity scattering with partial waves, the Lippmann-Schwinger equation or T-matrix, and zero-range boundary conditions to obtain bound states, scattering lengths and Friedel sums.

techniques.name: Topological band invariant calculations
techniques.scope: Compute Chern numbers, Z2 and winding invariants, Wilson-loop spectra and symmetry indicators of Bloch Hamiltonians to predict boundary modes and quantized responses.

techniques.name: Group theory and k·p symmetry analysis
techniques.scope: Use space-group representations, selection rules and invariant expansions to constrain effective Hamiltonians, degeneracies and allowed response tensors.

techniques.name: Holstein-Primakoff spin-wave expansion
techniques.scope: Expand spin operators in bosons around an ordered state and diagonalize the quadratic Hamiltonian to obtain magnon spectra and the 1/S corrections to order parameters and energies.

techniques.name: Parton and slave-particle constructions
techniques.scope: Fractionalize electrons or spins into partons coupled to emergent gauge fields, then analyze mean-field states and projective symmetry groups to characterize exotic phases.

techniques.name: Quadratic Hamiltonian diagonalization techniques
techniques.scope: Solve free-fermion or free-boson problems exactly with Jordan-Wigner mappings, Bogoliubov or Bogoliubov-de Gennes transformations, and transfer or correlation matrices.

techniques.name: Replica and cavity methods
techniques.scope: Average free energies over quenched disorder with replica or cavity/belief-propagation calculations to obtain thresholds, capacities and glass-transition lines.

techniques.name: Random-matrix and nonlinear sigma-model methods
techniques.scope: Use Gaussian ensembles, Dyson Brownian motion or supersymmetric and replica sigma models to compute level statistics, spectral form factors and localization corrections.

techniques.name: Conformal field theory methods
techniques.scope: Use conformal invariance (central charges, scaling dimensions, boundary CFT, modular invariance) to extract universal critical data and finite-size spectra.

techniques.name: Chern-Simons and K-matrix theory
techniques.scope: Describe topological phases with Chern-Simons effective actions and K-matrices to derive Hall conductances, anyon statistics, edge content and ground-state degeneracies.

techniques.name: Ginzburg-Landau and Gross-Pitaevskii functional analysis
techniques.scope: Minimize or linearize phenomenological or mean-field energy functionals to obtain critical fields, vortex and soliton structures, collective modes and phase boundaries.

techniques.name: Effective Hamiltonians via Schrieffer-Wolff and Magnus expansions
techniques.scope: Eliminate high-energy or fast degrees of freedom with degenerate perturbation theory or the high-frequency Floquet expansion to derive low-energy couplings and exchange constants.

techniques.name: Keldysh and Lindblad nonequilibrium methods
techniques.scope: Treat driven, dissipative or open systems with Keldysh contour field theory or quantum master equations to obtain steady states, decay rates and Liouvillian gaps.

subtopics.name: Inflation and primordial perturbations
subtopics.scope: Dynamics of the inflationary epoch and the statistics of the scalar and tensor perturbations it seeds, including reheating and primordial non-Gaussianity.

subtopics.name: CMB anisotropies and spectral distortions
subtopics.scope: Temperature and polarization anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background and departures of its spectrum from a blackbody, from recombination through secondary effects.

subtopics.name: Thermal history and cosmological relics
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium and its breakdown in the hot early universe: neutrino decoupling, Big Bang nucleosynthesis, and the freeze-out or freeze-in of relic particles.

subtopics.name: Large-scale structure and halo formation
subtopics.scope: Growth of matter density fluctuations from the linear to the nonlinear regime, and the abundance, clustering and internal structure of dark matter halos.

subtopics.name: Intergalactic medium and cosmic reionization
subtopics.scope: The thermal and ionization state of diffuse gas between galaxies, the absorption and emission signatures it leaves, and the reionization of hydrogen and helium.

subtopics.name: Gravitational lensing across mass scales
subtopics.scope: Deflection of light by stars, galaxies, clusters and the cosmic web, including image configurations, magnification, time delays and cosmic shear statistics.

subtopics.name: Black hole perturbations and quasinormal modes
subtopics.scope: Linear response of black hole spacetimes to test fields and metric perturbations, including ringdown spectra, tidal response, superradiance and absorption.

subtopics.name: Compact binary dynamics and gravitational waves
subtopics.scope: Conservative and dissipative dynamics of inspiraling black hole and neutron star binaries, and the gravitational waveforms and fluxes they emit.

subtopics.name: Modified and alternative theories of gravity
subtopics.scope: Extensions of general relativity such as scalar-tensor, f(R), Horndeski and massive gravity, their black hole and cosmological solutions, and their observational constraints.

subtopics.name: Neutron stars and dense matter
subtopics.scope: Structure, oscillations, magnetospheres and thermal and rotational evolution of neutron stars and pulsars as probes of matter above nuclear density.

subtopics.name: Accretion flows onto compact objects
subtopics.scope: Hydrodynamics and MHD of gas accreting onto black holes, neutron stars and white dwarfs, from spherical Bondi flow to thin and advection-dominated disks and their winds.

subtopics.name: High-energy astrophysics, transients and astroparticles
subtopics.scope: Explosive and high-energy phenomena and the particles they produce, including supernova explosions and remnants, gamma-ray bursts, fast radio bursts, tidal disruption events and other transients, relativistic jets and pulsar winds, particle acceleration by shocks and magnetic reconnection, non-thermal radiation processes, and the origin, propagation and detection of cosmic rays, high-energy neutrinos and very-high-energy gamma rays.

subtopics.name: Stellar interiors, oscillations and tides
subtopics.scope: Hydrostatic structure and evolution of stars, including convection and rotation, the global oscillation modes probed by asteroseismology, and tidal interaction in close binaries.

subtopics.name: Solar and stellar magnetohydrodynamics
subtopics.scope: Generation, transport and dissipation of magnetic fields in the Sun and other stars, including dynamos, flux tubes, coronal heating, MHD waves and magnetized winds.

subtopics.name: Galactic dynamics and stellar systems
subtopics.scope: Gravitational dynamics of galaxies and star clusters, including equilibrium distribution functions, orbits, disk instabilities, dynamical friction and collisional relaxation.

subtopics.name: Star formation and interstellar medium
subtopics.scope: Physics of the multiphase interstellar gas and its gravitational collapse into stars, including turbulence, thermal instability, magnetic support and protostellar collapse.

techniques.name: Gauge-invariant cosmological perturbation theory
techniques.scope: Linearizing the Einstein, fluid and Boltzmann equations about an FRW background in gauge-invariant variables to get growth rates, transfer functions and conserved quantities on super- and sub-horizon scales.

techniques.name: Mode functions, Bogoliubov coefficients, in-in correlators
techniques.scope: Quantizing fields on expanding or black hole backgrounds, solving their mode equations, and computing particle production, power spectra or higher-point correlators with Bogoliubov transformations and the in-in formalism.

techniques.name: Boltzmann and Fokker-Planck kinetic equations
techniques.scope: Solving rate equations, moment hierarchies or diffusion equations for phase-space distributions to get freeze-out abundances, Kompaneets spectral evolution or momentum-space diffusion.

techniques.name: Post-Newtonian and multipolar expansions
techniques.scope: Expanding systematically in v/c and in multipole moments to compute the conservative dynamics, radiated fluxes and far-zone fields of gravitating systems.

techniques.name: Geodesic and effective-potential orbit analysis
techniques.scope: Reducing motion in symmetric spacetimes or potentials to effective potentials through conserved quantities, giving circular-orbit radii, epicyclic frequencies, precession rates, deflection angles and capture cross sections.

techniques.name: WKB, eikonal and geometric-optics approximations
techniques.scope: Short-wavelength asymptotics of wave equations to get mode spectra, transmission and tunnelling factors, eikonal quasinormal frequencies and light propagation.

techniques.name: Sturm-Liouville eigenmode problems and shooting
techniques.scope: Casting oscillation or perturbation equations with physical boundary conditions as eigenvalue problems, solved analytically in limits or by shooting, continued fractions or spectral methods.

techniques.name: Matched asymptotic and multiple-scale expansions
techniques.scope: Joining inner and outer solutions across widely separated scales, or separating fast and slow time scales, to get leading corrections, boundary layers and secular evolution.

techniques.name: Self-similar solutions and shock jump conditions
techniques.scope: Reducing PDEs to ODEs through scaling symmetry (blast waves, collapse, winds) and joining regions with Newtonian or relativistic Rankine-Hugoniot conditions.

techniques.name: Linear stability and dispersion-relation analysis
techniques.scope: Perturbing an equilibrium with plane-wave or normal-mode ansatzes to derive dispersion relations, growth rates and critical thresholds such as the Jeans, Toomre, magnetorotational and thermal instabilities.

techniques.name: Hydrostatic equilibrium and polytropic models
techniques.scope: Solving the Lane-Emden, TOV or isothermal-sphere equations, together with virial and scaling arguments, to get mass-radius relations, maximum masses and structural constants.

techniques.name: Hamiltonian, action-angle and secular perturbation theory
techniques.scope: Using canonical transformations, orbit averaging and resonance analysis to compute precession rates, secular oscillations such as von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai cycles, resonance widths and diffusion coefficients.

techniques.name: Gaussian random field and excursion-set statistics
techniques.scope: Computing power spectra, correlation functions, variances, and peak or threshold statistics of Gaussian or weakly non-Gaussian fields with Wick's theorem, window functions and barrier-crossing arguments.

techniques.name: Radiative processes and radiative transfer
techniques.scope: Deriving emissivities, absorption coefficients, spectra and optical depths for synchrotron, Compton, bremsstrahlung and line processes, and solving the transfer equation in simple geometries.

subtopics.name: Lipid membrane elasticity and vesicle shapes
subtopics.scope: Curvature elasticity, thermal undulations and shape changes of lipid bilayers, vesicles and red blood cells, including deformations caused by membrane proteins and inclusions.

subtopics.name: Semiflexible polymer mechanics of DNA and chromatin
subtopics.scope: Elasticity and statistical mechanics of DNA, chromatin fibers and stiff biofilaments under force, torque, confinement and looping constraints.

subtopics.name: Molecular motors and Brownian ratchets
subtopics.scope: Stochastic models of motor proteins and ratchet mechanisms that turn chemical free energy into directed motion, including force-velocity relations, efficiency and thermodynamic bounds.

subtopics.name: Active gels and cytoskeletal active matter
subtopics.scope: Continuum hydrodynamic theories of actomyosin cortices, microtubule-motor mixtures and active nematics, including spontaneous flows, defect dynamics and activity-driven instabilities.

subtopics.name: Microswimmer hydrodynamics at low Reynolds number
subtopics.scope: Propulsion, flow fields, interactions and navigation of flagellated cells, ciliated organisms and model swimmers in viscous fluids.

subtopics.name: Stochastic gene regulatory dynamics and cell fate
subtopics.scope: Covers noise and nonlinear dynamics in gene regulatory and intracellular biochemical networks: transcriptional bursting and copy-number statistics, chemical master equation methods, bistability and epigenetic landscapes, genetic oscillators and circadian clocks, cell-fate decisions, and the statistics of cell growth, size control and division.

subtopics.name: Physical limits of biochemical sensing and proofreading
subtopics.scope: Accuracy, energy cost and information capacity of receptor-based sensing, signaling cascades and kinetic proofreading in molecular recognition.

subtopics.name: Reaction-diffusion patterning and morphogen gradients
subtopics.scope: How spatial patterns in development and inside cells form, scale and stay robust under reaction-diffusion and mechanochemical mechanisms.

subtopics.name: Population genetics of selection and drift
subtopics.scope: Stochastic dynamics of allele frequencies under mutation, selection, drift and recombination, including fixation, the speed of adaptation and genealogies.

subtopics.name: Epidemic spreading and outbreak thresholds
subtopics.scope: Compartmental, network and stochastic models of infectious disease transmission, covering thresholds, final epidemic sizes and control strategies.

subtopics.name: Ecological community dynamics and stability
subtopics.scope: Dynamics, coexistence and stability of interacting species, from predator-prey and competition models to large random ecosystems.

subtopics.name: Electrostatics of biomolecules and polyelectrolytes
subtopics.scope: Screening, counterion condensation and charge-mediated interactions of DNA, proteins, membranes and other charged soft matter in ionic solutions.

subtopics.name: Diffusive search and first-passage kinetics in cells
subtopics.scope: Kinetics of molecules and particles finding targets by diffusion, including facilitated diffusion of transcription factors, narrow escape and intermittent search strategies.

subtopics.name: Protein folding and conformational transitions
subtopics.scope: Statistical mechanics of folding, helix-coil and unfolding transitions in proteins and nucleic acids, including energy landscapes, cooperativity and force spectroscopy.

techniques.name: Linear stability and dispersion relations
techniques.scope: Linearize ODE or PDE models about homogeneous or steady states to get growth rates, critical parameters and the wavelengths that instabilities select.

techniques.name: Backward equations for first-passage problems
techniques.scope: Solve backward Kolmogorov or Fokker-Planck equations with absorbing boundaries to get fixation probabilities, splitting probabilities and mean first-passage times.

techniques.name: Generating functions for master equations
techniques.scope: Turn chemical or birth-death master equations into PDEs for generating functions to get exact stationary distributions, moments and time-dependent solutions.

techniques.name: Linear noise approximation and system-size expansion
techniques.scope: Use van Kampen's expansion in inverse system size to get Gaussian fluctuations, covariance matrices from Lyapunov equations, and noise power spectra.

techniques.name: WKB and large-deviation asymptotics
techniques.scope: Use eikonal or Hamiltonian approximations for rare events to get exponentially small rates, such as mean extinction times, switching rates and optimal escape paths.

techniques.name: Transfer matrices for one-dimensional lattice models
techniques.scope: Get partition functions, correlation lengths and transition curves of linear chain models from the leading eigenvalues of transfer matrices.

techniques.name: Variational shape equations from elastic energies
techniques.scope: Minimize curvature, bending or elastic free energies to derive Euler-Lagrange shape equations, equilibrium configurations and buckling or budding thresholds.

techniques.name: Gaussian fluctuation spectra via normal modes
techniques.scope: Expand quadratic Hamiltonians of membranes, filaments or fields in Fourier modes and use equipartition to get fluctuation spectra, correlation functions and entropic forces.

techniques.name: Stokes-flow singularities and reciprocal theorem
techniques.scope: Use Stokeslet and multipole expansions, resistive-force and slender-body theory, and the Lorentz reciprocal theorem to compute swimming speeds, drag coefficients and flow fields.

techniques.name: Steady states of kinetic Markov networks
techniques.scope: Solve discrete-state kinetic schemes, for example with matrix-tree (King-Altman) methods, to get steady-state fluxes, motor velocities, error fractions and entropy production rates.

techniques.name: Random matrix and cavity methods
techniques.scope: Apply random-matrix spectra and cavity or replica self-consistency to large random interaction systems to get stability bounds, surviving-species fractions and abundance statistics.

techniques.name: Mean-field and Poisson-Boltzmann theory
techniques.scope: Solve self-consistent mean-field equations, including nonlinear Poisson-Boltzmann solutions, to get free energies, screened potentials, condensed counterion fractions and phase boundaries.

subtopics.name: Hydrodynamic stability of shear flows
subtopics.scope: Linear, non-modal and nonlinear instability and transition of parallel and nearly parallel flows such as channel, pipe, Couette, jet, wake and mixing-layer flows.

subtopics.name: Buoyancy-driven convection, plumes and mixing
subtopics.scope: Flows driven by density or surface-tension differences: Rayleigh-Bénard, horizontal, internally heated, penetrative, Marangoni and double-diffusive convection, magnetoconvection and non-Oberbeck-Boussinesq effects, plus buoyant plumes, thermals and Rayleigh-Taylor mixing, covering how they start, the patterns and large-scale circulations they form, and how heat, mass and buoyancy transport scale with control parameters.

subtopics.name: Rotating and stratified geophysical flows
subtopics.scope: Dynamics of rotating and density-stratified fluids in atmospheres and oceans, including quasi-geostrophic dynamics, Rossby and inertia-gravity waves, Ekman layers and baroclinic instability.

subtopics.name: Low-Reynolds-number flows and microswimmers
subtopics.scope: Stokes flow around particles, filaments and self-propelled microorganisms, including suspension rheology, hydrodynamic interactions, mobility problems and swimming kinematics.

subtopics.name: Thin liquid films and lubrication
subtopics.scope: Viscous films and lubricated layers on substrates or in narrow gaps, including coating, spreading, dewetting, rupture, contact-line motion and viscous gravity currents.

subtopics.name: Drops, bubbles and capillary instabilities
subtopics.scope: Interfaces driven by surface tension, including jet breakup, pinch-off, drop and bubble oscillation, coalescence, and Rayleigh-Taylor and Faraday interfacial instabilities.

subtopics.name: Nonlinear water waves and solitons
subtopics.scope: Surface and interfacial gravity-capillary waves and their weakly nonlinear model equations, including steep periodic waves, modulational instability, solitary waves and wave-wave resonances.

subtopics.name: Turbulence cascades and intermittency
subtopics.scope: Statistical theory of homogeneous turbulence in two and three dimensions, including energy and enstrophy cascades, structure functions, passive-scalar mixing and shell models.

subtopics.name: Boundary layers and wall-bounded flows
subtopics.scope: Laminar and turbulent boundary layers, separation and near-wall flow structure, including similarity profiles, triple-deck interaction theory and logarithmic-law scaling in channels and pipes.

subtopics.name: Vortex dynamics and point vortices
subtopics.scope: Motion, interaction and stability of concentrated vorticity, including point-vortex systems, vortex patches, rings, filaments and vortex streets.

subtopics.name: Compressible flows and shock waves
subtopics.scope: Gas dynamics at finite Mach number, including shock structure, Riemann problems, nozzle flows, blast waves, shock-driven interfacial instabilities and aeroacoustic sound generation.

subtopics.name: Porous, granular and non-Newtonian flows
subtopics.scope: Flows through and of complex or heterogeneous media, including Darcy and Hele-Shaw flows, viscous fingering and displacement fronts, Laplacian growth, convection and dispersion in porous layers, poroelasticity, dense granular flows and their rheology, and viscoelastic, yield-stress and other non-Newtonian fluid flows.

subtopics.name: Chaotic advection and Lagrangian transport
subtopics.scope: Mixing and transport of passive tracers by laminar, time-dependent flows, including Lagrangian coherent structures, transport barriers, lobe dynamics and chaotic stirring.

subtopics.name: Low-dimensional chaos and bifurcations
subtopics.scope: Chaotic dynamics of maps, ODE models and coupled oscillators, including routes to chaos, strange attractors, Lyapunov spectra, Hamiltonian chaos and synchronization.

techniques.name: Normal-mode and Floquet stability analysis
techniques.scope: Linearizing about a steady or time-periodic base state and solving the resulting eigenvalue problem (dispersion relation, Orr-Sommerfeld, Mathieu/Floquet) for growth rates, neutral curves and critical parameters.

techniques.name: Weakly nonlinear amplitude equation derivation
techniques.scope: Using multiple scales, center-manifold or normal-form reduction near onset to derive Landau or Ginzburg-Landau equations and compute their coefficients, saturation amplitudes and bifurcation type.

techniques.name: Matched asymptotic and WKB expansions
techniques.scope: Building inner and outer or WKB approximations in a small parameter and matching them to obtain leading-order corrections, scaling laws and asymptotic eigenvalue conditions.

techniques.name: Long-wave lubrication and thin-layer reductions
techniques.scope: Using a small aspect ratio to reduce the Navier-Stokes equations to evolution equations for film thickness or layer depth, then analyzing their steady states, stability and dynamics.

techniques.name: Self-similar solutions and scaling exponents
techniques.scope: Reducing PDEs via similarity variables to ODEs and finding first- or second-kind similarity exponents and prefactors through nonlinear eigenvalue or phase-plane analysis.

techniques.name: Complex-variable and conformal mapping methods
techniques.scope: Solving two-dimensional potential, Stokes or Hele-Shaw problems with complex potentials, conformal maps and Schwarz functions to obtain exact flow fields, forces and free-boundary shapes.

techniques.name: Stokes singularities and reciprocal theorems
techniques.scope: Representing low-Reynolds-number flows with Stokeslets, multipoles and image systems, and using the Lorentz reciprocal theorem or Faxén laws to obtain drag, mobilities and swimming velocities.

techniques.name: Integrable methods and exact soliton solutions
techniques.scope: Applying inverse scattering, Hirota bilinear forms, Bäcklund transformations or traveling-wave quadrature to nonlinear wave equations to obtain soliton amplitudes, speeds and conserved quantities.

techniques.name: Energy stability and variational bounds
techniques.scope: Using energy functionals, Euler-Lagrange equations and the background-field method to derive rigorous stability thresholds and upper bounds on transport quantities such as dissipation or Nusselt number.

techniques.name: Exact statistical relations and turbulence closures
techniques.scope: Deriving exact results from Kármán-Howarth-type balances, or solving tractable models such as the Kraichnan ensemble and spectral closures, to obtain structure-function laws, constants and anomalous exponents.

techniques.name: Characteristics and shock jump conditions
techniques.scope: Solving hyperbolic conservation laws with characteristics, Riemann invariants and Rankine-Hugoniot conditions to find wave speeds, shock strengths, breaking times and Riemann-problem solutions.

techniques.name: Melnikov, Lyapunov and periodic-orbit methods
techniques.scope: Quantifying chaos and transport in low-dimensional systems through Melnikov integrals, Lyapunov exponents, periodic-orbit and symbolic-dynamics analysis, and renormalization of bifurcation cascades.

subtopics.name: Hamiltonian chaos and KAM theory
subtopics.scope: How invariant tori break up, how resonances overlap, and how mixed phase space is organized in near-integrable Hamiltonian flows and in area-preserving or symplectic maps.

subtopics.name: Deterministic diffusion and anomalous chaotic transport
subtopics.scope: Transport coefficients and normal, sub- or superdiffusive spreading produced by deterministic chaotic maps, Lorentz gases and intermittent dynamics.

subtopics.name: Transient chaos and open dynamical systems
subtopics.scope: Escape from chaotic saddles in open maps, billiards and scattering systems, including escape rates, fractal repellers and fractal basin boundaries.

subtopics.name: Quantum chaos and spectral statistics
subtopics.scope: Signatures of classical chaos in quantum systems, including level statistics, semiclassical periodic-orbit theory, dynamical localization and scrambling.

subtopics.name: Piecewise-smooth and impacting dynamical systems
subtopics.scope: Dynamics and bifurcations of systems with switching, impacts or friction, including border-collision, grazing and sliding phenomena.

subtopics.name: Bifurcations and multiple-timescale dynamics in flows
subtopics.scope: Local and global bifurcations of low-dimensional dissipative ODEs and their slow-fast structure, including normal forms, homoclinic orbits, canards and mixed-mode oscillations.

subtopics.name: Synchronization and mode locking of oscillators
subtopics.scope: How limit-cycle oscillators lock to periodic forcing or to each other, from Arnold tongues and circle maps to collective synchronization in large populations and networks.

subtopics.name: Noise-induced phenomena in nonlinear systems
subtopics.scope: How random fluctuations change nonlinear dynamics, including stochastic and coherence resonance, noise-induced transitions and escape, and phase diffusion of noisy oscillators.

subtopics.name: Delay-differential equations and delayed feedback
subtopics.scope: Stability, bifurcations and chaos in systems with time-delayed coupling or feedback, including oscillations caused by delay and chaos control by delayed feedback.

subtopics.name: Self-organized criticality and avalanche dynamics
subtopics.scope: Systems that reach critical states on their own and show scale-free avalanches, including sandpile models, branching processes and extremal dynamics.

subtopics.name: Turing patterns and amplitude equations
subtopics.scope: Instabilities of homogeneous states in reaction-diffusion and other spatially extended systems, and the weakly nonlinear selection, stability and dynamics of stripes, hexagons and other patterns.

subtopics.name: Modulational instability and nonlinear dispersive waves
subtopics.scope: Evolution of nonlinear dispersive wave fields governed by NLS-, KdV- and related equations, including modulational instability, rogue waves and dispersive shock waves.

subtopics.name: Discrete breathers and nonlinear lattice dynamics
subtopics.scope: Localized excitations, energy transport and thermalization in nonlinear lattices such as discrete NLS, Klein-Gordon and Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chains.

subtopics.name: Fronts and localized dissipative structures
subtopics.scope: Propagating fronts, pulses and stationary localized states in dissipative extended systems, including front speed selection, excitable waves and homoclinic snaking.

techniques.name: Linear stability and dispersion relation analysis
techniques.scope: Linearize about a steady, uniform or periodic state and solve the eigenvalue problem, dispersion relation or transcendental (delay) characteristic equation to get growth rates, critical wavenumbers and instability thresholds.

techniques.name: Center manifold and normal form reduction
techniques.scope: Reduce the dynamics near a bifurcation to its center manifold and compute normal-form coefficients, such as the first Lyapunov coefficient, which determine criticality, amplitude scaling and unfolding structure.

techniques.name: Multiple-scale perturbation and averaging methods
techniques.scope: Separate fast and slow time or space scales using multiple-scales, Krylov-Bogoliubov averaging or Poincare-Lindstedt expansions to derive amplitude equations, frequency shifts and resonance conditions.

techniques.name: Floquet theory and parametric stability
techniques.scope: Compute monodromy matrices, Floquet multipliers or Hill determinants to find the stability of periodic orbits and the boundaries of parametric-resonance tongues.

techniques.name: Melnikov and separatrix-splitting analysis
techniques.scope: Evaluate Melnikov integrals along unperturbed separatrices to get thresholds for transverse homoclinic intersections, exponentially small splitting angles or the onset of chaotic escape.

techniques.name: Phase reduction of limit-cycle oscillators
techniques.scope: Reduce weakly perturbed or coupled oscillators to phase equations using isochrons and phase response curves, then predict locking ranges, Arnold tongue widths and synchronization thresholds.

techniques.name: Self-consistent mean-field and Ott-Antonsen reduction
techniques.scope: Close the dynamics of large oscillator or agent populations with self-consistency equations or low-dimensional invariant-manifold ansatzes to get order parameters, critical couplings and bifurcation diagrams.

techniques.name: Transfer operators and invariant densities
techniques.scope: Build Perron-Frobenius operators, Markov partitions or invariant densities of chaotic maps and use them to compute Lyapunov exponents, entropies, correlation decay, escape rates and diffusion coefficients.

techniques.name: Symbolic dynamics and periodic-orbit expansions
techniques.scope: Encode orbits symbolically to count periodic orbits and compute topological entropy, then evaluate dynamical zeta functions, cycle expansions or semiclassical trace formulas for averages and spectra.

techniques.name: Fokker-Planck and first-passage analysis
techniques.scope: Solve stationary Fokker-Planck or backward Kolmogorov equations, often with Kramers or WKB asymptotics, to get stationary distributions, mean escape times and the response of the system to noise.

techniques.name: Exact traveling-wave and soliton construction
techniques.scope: Construct exact or asymptotic solitons, fronts and periodic waves through traveling-wave reduction, phase-plane analysis or ansatz methods, and extract their speeds, widths, amplitudes and existence conditions.

techniques.name: Renormalization-group and scaling analysis
techniques.scope: Derive universal constants, critical exponents and scaling laws by renormalizing maps or orbits, analyzing self-similar bifurcation cascades, or applying scaling arguments near critical points.
